signals.title: feat(databricks): add new Claude models and cached token pricing
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Databricks Claude Opus 4.8, Opus 5, Sonnet 5 unpriced, spend logged as $0 - Databricks entries carried no cached token pricing - Databricks cost tracking billed cached tokens at full input rate How it solves it: - Adds the missing Databricks Claude entries with DBU and USD rates - Adds cache write and cache read rates to every Databricks proprietary chat model - Routes Databricks cost tracking through the shared cache aware calculator ## User Flow Before: a team running Databricks hosted Claude with prompt caching sees $0 spend on the newest models, and inflated spend on the older ones 1. They call POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "databricks/databricks-claude-opus-5"` and a cached system prompt 2. The response comes back fine and reports 8000 cache read tokens plus 2000 cache write tokens 3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and the request is logged at $0 spend, so the model is invisible in cost reporting 4. They repeat the same call against `databricks/databricks-claude-opus-4-6`, which is priced, and the log shows $0.0675 for 11000 prompt and 500 completion tokens 5. That figure charges all 11000 prompt tokens at the full input rate, so caching looks like it saved nothing After: the newest models are priced, and cached tokens bill at Databricks cache rates 1. They call POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "databricks/databricks-claude-opus-5"` and a cached system prompt 2. The response comes back fine and reports 8000 cache read tokens plus 2000 cache write tokens 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs now shows that request at $0.034, matching the published Databricks rates 4. They repeat the same call against `databricks/databricks-claude-opus-4-6` and the log shows $0.034 instead of $0.0675 5. The 8000 cached tokens bill at the cache read rate and the 2000 written tokens at the cache write rate, so caching shows up as real savings ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5977 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Rates come from https://www.databricks.com/product/pricing/proprietary-foundation-model-serving at 1 DBU = $0.07, and context windows from https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/machine-learning/foundation-model-apis/supported-models There is no Databricks workspace credential on this machine, so the spend a user would see is captured through the live proxy's own cost endpoint with the exact usage shape Databricks returns for a cached request, rather than by paying for a call A screen recording of the cached request billing through the Admin UI logs page, captured at f5cb5619d0, is posted in the [Slack thread](https://berriaillm.slack.com/archives/C0BE49SAUE6/p1787353730147759?thread_ts=1787353730.147759&cid=C0BE49SAUE6) with the log detail screenshots. The before run below was captured at 66b930b540 and the after run at f5cb5619d0 Shared setup, run once per revision: ```bash cat > /tmp/dbx_config.yaml <<'EOF' model_list: - model_name: dbx-claude-opus-5 litellm_params: model: databricks/databricks-claude-opus-5 api_key: fake-key api_base: https://example.cloud.databricks.com general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 EOF LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config /tmp/dbx_config.yaml --detailed_debug cost() { curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/spend/calculate \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"completion_response":{"id":"c1","object":"chat.completion","created":1,"model":"databricks/'"$1"'","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"hi"},"finish_reason":"stop"}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":11000,"completion_tokens":500,"total_tokens":11500,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2000,"cache_read_input_tokens":8000}}}'; echo; } ``` ### Before (66b930b540) #### newest Claude models 1. `cost databricks-claude-opus-5` -> `{"cost":0.0}` 2. `cost databricks-claude-sonnet-5` -> `{"cost":0.0}` #### cached tokens on an already priced model 1. `cost databricks-claude-opus-4-6` -> `{"cost":0.067500335}` 2. That is all 11000 prompt tokens at $5.00/M plus 500 output tokens at $25.00/M, with the 8000 cache reads and 2000 cache writes charged as fresh input ### After (f5cb5619d0) #### newest Claude models 1. `cost databricks-claude-opus-5` -> `{"cost":0.034000134}` 2. `cost databricks-claude-sonnet-5` -> `{"cost":0.013599866000000002}` #### cached tokens on an already priced model 1. `cost databricks-claude-opus-4-6` -> `{"cost":0.034000134}` 2. That is 1000 fresh input tokens at $5.00/M, 2000 cache writes at $6.25/M, 8000 cache reads at $0.50/M, and 500 output tokens at $25.00/M #### cached tokens end to end through the Admin UI 1. Same 11000 prompt / 500 completion request with 8000 cache reads and 2000 cache writes, driven from the Playground against a mock upstream aliased to `databricks/databricks-claude-opus-5` 2. http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs logs it at `$0.034000`, and the Cost Breakdown itemises Input `$0.00500003`, Prompt Cache Read `$0.00400002` (8,000 tokens), Prompt Cache Write `$0.01250008` (2,000 tokens), Output `$0.01250001` 3. The no cache twin of that request logs `$0.067500`, billing all 11,000 prompt tokens at the input rate ## Type 🆕 New Feature 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Sonnet 5 introductory rates hold through 2026-08-31, then standard rates apply - Cache rates for Gemini and GPT-5 entries follow the same published table - Legacy `dbrx-instruct` and `meta-llama-3.1-70b` aliases point at registry keys that no longer exist, kept as is - The new Claude entries also carry the adaptive thinking, sampling param, and cache minimum flags their Anthropic counterparts already had, which CI enforces - `test_fallback_generalizations` moved its unmapped Databricks id off `databricks-claude-opus-5-1`, which is no longer unmapped now that Opus 5 is in the registry - The UI run used a mock upstream, so the Gemini and GPT-5 Databricks entries were priced through `/spend/calculate` only, not through real provider traffic ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/564d0e383a354b73b0c83aefa1e814b2

signals.title: test(e2e): pin the openai websocket passthrough prefixes
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The websocket passthrough fix shipped with no e2e coverage - Both OpenAI prefixes could go back to refusing every upgrade - Realtime and `responses.connect` clients would break unnoticed How it solves it: - Two live tests driving a real websocket client, not HTTP - The realtime one reads OpenAI's own `session.created` frame back - Proven red with the routes unregistered, green with them ## User Flow Before: a realtime or `client.responses.connect()` app cannot open a socket through the gateway at all, so that traffic has to route around it 1. The user mints a key for their voice app: `POST https://litellm-domain/key/generate` with `{"models": []}`, and gets back an `sk-...` key 2. They check the prefix over HTTP first: `POST https://litellm-domain/openai_passthrough/v1/responses` with `Authorization: Bearer sk-...` and `{"model": "gpt-5.5", "input": "hi"}`, and get a 200 carrying a `resp_...` id 3. They point the app's realtime session at the same prefix: websocket upgrade `GET wss://litellm-domain/openai_passthrough/v1/realtime?model=gpt-realtime-2` with `Authorization: Bearer sk-...`, and get back `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden`. No socket opens and the response carries no message 4. They try the SDK's `client.responses.connect()` against the other prefix: websocket upgrade `GET wss://litellm-domain/openai/v1/responses`, and get the same bare `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden` 5. They retry with the master key, then with a key scoped to every model, and every upgrade comes back 403 in exactly the same way, with nothing in the response to say what was wrong 6. They give up on the gateway for this app and connect straight to `wss://api.openai.com/v1/realtime` with their own OpenAI key. Those sessions never appear in `GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs`, and the key's budget and rate limits never apply to them Any other user hits the identical 403 no matter what their key is allowed to reach, because the refusal never looks at the key After: the same app opens the socket and talks to the model through the gateway 1. The user mints a key for their voice app: `POST https://litellm-domain/key/generate` with `{"models": []}`, and gets back an `sk-...` key 2. They check the prefix over HTTP first: `POST https://litellm-domain/openai_passthrough/v1/responses` with `Authorization: Bearer sk-...` and `{"model": "gpt-5.5", "input": "hi"}`, and get a 200 carrying a `resp_...` id 3. They point the app's realtime session at the same prefix: websocket upgrade `GET wss://litellm-domain/openai_passthrough/v1/realtime?model=gpt-realtime-2` with `Authorization: Bearer sk-...`, and get `HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols`. The first frame they read is OpenAI's own `{"type": "session.created", ...}` 4. They send and receive audio and text events over that socket for the rest of the session, against the same key their HTTP traffic uses 5. `client.responses.connect()` against `wss://litellm-domain/openai/v1/responses` also returns `HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols`, and the socket stays open waiting for the app's first event 6. Their realtime traffic runs through the gateway, so it is billed to the same key rather than to a separate OpenAI credential the gateway never sees Another user whose key is scoped to a subset of models is still refused the upgrade with a 403, so they cannot reach a model outside their allow-list over the socket either ## Relevant issues Pins the fix for #36088 ## Linear ticket Part of LIT-5902. This covers the PT-03 row; the PT-10 row stays open on that ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The fix being pinned (#36151) is already on the merge base, so a Before captured there would be green and would prove nothing. Before is therefore the PR tip with that fix's two route registrations removed, which is exactly what the file looked like before #36151 landed. That is the only difference between the two sides Shared setup: a proxy from this branch on `http://localhost:43127` against a local Postgres, `gpt-5.5` and `gemini-2.5-flash` registered from config, keys minted with `POST /key/generate`. The realtime traffic hits real OpenAI ### Before (9b27d7a977, with the websocket routes unregistered) 1. Deleted the two `@router.websocket` lines at `litellm/proxy/pass_through_endpoints/llm_passthrough_endpoints.py:2152-2153` and rebooted the proxy 2. `uv run pytest llm_translation/test_passthrough_e2e.py -k TestOpenAIPassthroughWebsocket` -> `2 failed, 12 deselected in 0.73s`, with `AssertionError: /openai/v1/responses refused the websocket upgrade with HTTP 403; the prefix relays this route over HTTP but drops a responses.connect client before the socket opens` 3. A raw client sees the same thing, so the failure is the route and not the test: connecting to `ws://localhost:43127/openai_passthrough/v1/realtime?model=gpt-realtime-2` with an all-models key raises `InvalidStatus: server rejected WebSocket connection: HTTP 403` ### After (9b27d7a977, the PR tip) 1. Restored the file, rebooted the proxy, and re-ran the same command -> `2 passed, 12 deselected in 2.73s` 2. The same raw client probe at this commit, across both prefixes and both key shapes: ``` all-models /openai_passthrough/v1/realtime?model=gpt-realtime-2: HANDSHAKE ACCEPTED first frame type='session.created' keys=['event_id', 'session', 'type'] restricted /openai_passthrough/v1/realtime?model=gpt-realtime-2: HANDSHAKE REJECTED http=403 all-models /openai/v1/responses: HANDSHAKE ACCEPTED restricted /openai/v1/responses: HANDSHAKE REJECTED http=403 all-models /openai_passthrough/v1/responses: HANDSHAKE ACCEPTED restricted /openai_passthrough/v1/responses: HANDSHAKE REJECTED http=403 no-such-prefix /nonexistent_prefix/v1/realtime: HANDSHAKE REJECTED http=403 ``` 3. `make check` -> `PASS`, which runs `basedpyright tests/e2e` -> `0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes` and the raw HTTP client ban 4. `uv run pytest llm_translation/realtime/ --collect-only -q` -> `9 tests collected`, so moving `ws_base_url` did not break the suite it came from 5. `uv run pytest coverage_registry/test_collector.py -q` -> `13 passed`, and `uv run python -m coverage_registry.collector` prints no "marker(s) point at ids not in the registry" line, so both new `covers` ids resolve to the rows added here ## Type ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) - The responses leg asserts only that the upgrade was accepted - `/openai/v1/realtime` is not testable, the app-level route claims it - `gpt-realtime-2` is a literal in the test module - The ticket's stated 1008/1011 signal was wrong, corrected here - `buildkite/e2e-tests` is red on three pre-existing failures outside this diff OpenAI speaks first on realtime, which is why that test can assert a `session.created` frame and prove the socket was really relayed upstream. A `responses.connect` socket waits for the client, so there is no opening frame to read and the accepted handshake is the whole signal. It still catches the regression exactly, since that route answered 403 before the fix, but it does not prove the relay the way the realtime one does The second prefix is exercised through `/openai/v1/responses` rather than `/openai/v1/realtime`, which issue #36088 also lists. The app-level realtime endpoint in `proxy_server.py` is registered before the passthrough router is included, so it wins that path and the passthrough route never sees it. Testing `/openai/v1/realtime` would assert the app-level endpoint instead, which is a different behavior `REALTIME_MODEL` sits in the test module as a literal, the same way `EMBEDDING_MODEL` already does. The passthrough route relays the model name to OpenAI verbatim, so it has to be OpenAI's own name rather than a gateway alias, but an environment that needs a different realtime model has no way to say so LIT-5902 states the signal is a handshake accepted and then closed with 1008 or 1011. That is not what happens. The websocket auth dependency and the model-restriction check both close before `accept()`, and Starlette turns a pre-accept close into an HTTP 403 handshake rejection, which is indistinguishable from the unregistered route's 403. The After probe above shows it directly: the restricted key gets the same 403 as the nonexistent prefix. The usable signal is an all-models key getting an accepted handshake, which is what these tests assert `buildkite/e2e-tests` is red here, and none of it comes from this change. Editing `e2e_config.py` makes the gate select the entire e2e suite instead of a subset, so this is one of the few builds that runs these three tests at all, which is why every neighbouring build is green. Both new tests passed in that same run. The failures are `test_unflagged_model_converts_system_reminder_and_succeeds` in `TestAzureFoundryMidConversationSystem`, `TestVertexMidConversationSystem`, and `TestBedrockInvokeMidConversationSystem`, each of which has now failed 16 of 16 runs over the past seven days for a reliability of 0. All three wait up to 60 seconds for a provider prompt cache to become fully readable, and neither file they live in appears in this diff. They are already tracked as LIT-5921. The check is not required on `litellm_internal_staging` and every required check is green ## QA runbook - `tests/e2e/llm_translation/test_passthrough_e2e.py::TestOpenAIPassthroughWebsocket::test_realtime_upgrade_reaches_openai_through_the_passthrough_prefix` - a realtime client opens a socket on the dedicated prefix and reads OpenAI's opening session event - [ ] Mint an all-models key: `curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -d '{"models": []}'` (needs `OPENAI_API_KEY` on the proxy) - [ ] Open a websocket to `ws://localhost:4000/openai_passthrough/v1/realtime?model=gpt-realtime-2` with `Authorization: Bearer <key>` - [ ] Expect `101 Switching Protocols` and a first frame whose `type` is `session.created` - [ ] Repeat with a key restricted to one model and expect a `403` handshake rejection instead, which is the shape the unregistered route also returns - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey (e.g., assert actual expected spend instead of just spend > 0) or potentially flaky - `tests/e2e/llm_translation/test_passthrough_e2e.py::TestOpenAIPassthroughWebsocket::test_responses_upgrade_is_accepted_on_the_openai_prefix` - a `responses.connect` client is allowed to open a socket on the `/openai` prefix - [ ] Using the same all-models key, open a websocket to `ws://localhost:4000/openai/v1/responses` - [ ] Expect `101 Switching Protocols` and the socket to stay open with no frame arriving, since that route waits for the client to send first - signals.title: feat(terraform): add internal managed load balancer mode for GCP module
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Add INTERNAL_MANAGED support for the GCP Terraform load balancer path - Keep the existing EXTERNAL_MANAGED behavior unchanged for current users - Avoid broad refactors while enabling private internal load balancing How it solves it: - Adds `load_balancing_scheme` input and threads it through LB resources - Splits forwarding rules for EXTERNAL_MANAGED vs INTERNAL_MANAGED requirements - Adds proxy-only subnet support for internal managed Envoy proxy allocation - Gates HTTPS resources and managed cert flow to EXTERNAL_MANAGED only - Adds guardrails and docs to prevent invalid INTERNAL_MANAGED TLS configuration ## User Flow Before: users who needed an internal managed GCP load balancer could not configure this module to create one 1. They configure the module for GCP deployment and run `terraform apply` 2. The module always creates EXTERNAL_MANAGED LB resources 3. They receive a public external LB path instead of an internal managed private path After: users can choose internal managed mode with minimal extra inputs and keep existing external behavior 1. They set `load_balancing_scheme = "INTERNAL_MANAGED"` and run `terraform apply` 2. The module creates INTERNAL_MANAGED-compatible LB resources and forwarding rules 3. They receive a private internal LB frontend while existing EXTERNAL_MANAGED users keep current behavior ## Relevant issues Closes #37853 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [ ] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: 1. Terraform module: `terraform/litellm/gcp` 2. New mode input: `load_balancing_scheme` ### Before (merge-base) 1. Configure module for GCP and run plan/apply with internal-only intent 2. The module path provisions EXTERNAL_MANAGED LB resources only 3. Internal managed mode is not available through module inputs ### After (current branch tip) 1. Configure `load_balancing_scheme = "INTERNAL_MANAGED"` and run plan/apply 2. The module provisions INTERNAL_MANAGED-compatible LB resources including proxy-only subnet support 3. Configure `load_balancing_scheme = "EXTERNAL_MANAGED"` and optional `lb_domains` to keep current HTTPS behavior 4. INTERNAL_MANAGED plus non-empty `lb_domains` is blocked by explicit guardrails ## Type Infrastructure Documentation ## Caveats (if any) - TLS is intentionally supported only for EXTERNAL_MANAGED in this change - INTERNAL_MANAGED TLS uses a different certificate model and is deferred - Users with DNS-validated domains can add internal TLS via separate Certificate Manager configurations ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(otel): emit gen_ai.provider.name for metrics in semconv experimental mode
signals.text: ## Summary Fixes the emitted GenAI provider attribute in `OpenTelemetry._record_metrics()`: - When `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental` is active, metric histograms now emit `gen_ai.provider.name` (aligning with OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions) instead of the superseded `gen_ai.system`. - Added robust fallback to `kwargs.get("custom_llm_provider")` when not present in `litellm_params`. - Added unit test `test_record_metrics_semconv_provider_name`. ## Motivation Issue #36759: `gen_ai.system` is deprecated in current OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions and superseded by `gen_ai.provider.name`. When experimental semconv is enabled, metric records were still emitting the legacy `gen_ai.system` key, creating schema inconsistencies across metrics and trace spans. ## Changes - `litellm/integrations/opentelemetry.py`: Use `gen_ai.provider.name` for metric common attributes under experimental semconv mode. - `tests/logging_callback_tests/test_opentelemetry_unit_tests.py`: Added test assertion for metric attributes under both legacy and semconv modes. ## Tests - Added `test_record_metrics_semconv_provider_name` verifying attribute emission.

signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Repeated `foo[]` form keys lost every value but the last - Four more classes of test that cannot fail were ungated - The `get_form_data` test mocked a dict, reproducing the bug How it solves it: - Read the form multidict with `multi_items()`, not `dict()` - Gate the test tree on F601, B023, B025, F632 - Every `request.form` mock now returns real `FormData` ## User Flow Before: a developer transcribing audio asks for word and segment timestamps, and word timestamps never come back 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/transcriptions as multipart with `model=whisper-1`, `response_format=verbose_json`, `timestamp_granularities[]=word` and `timestamp_granularities[]=segment` 2. The response comes back 200 with `segments` populated and `words` set to `null` 3. Calling OpenAI directly with the identical form returns both, so the app's word-level captioning works everywhere except through the gateway After: the same request returns both granularities 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/transcriptions with both `timestamp_granularities[]` values 2. The response comes back 200 with `segments` populated and `words` carrying one entry per spoken word 3. Word-level captioning behaves the same through the gateway as it does against OpenAI ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. LiteLLM keeps every timestamp granularity."` ```yaml model_list: - model_name: whisper-1 litellm_params: model: openai/whisper-1 api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: sk-qa-1234 ``` ### Before (a59e6115ba) 1. Ask for both granularities on one request ```console $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4577/v1/audio/transcriptions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-1234" \ -F "model=whisper-1" -F "file=@speech.m4a" -F "response_format=verbose_json" \ -F "timestamp_granularities[]=word" -F "timestamp_granularities[]=segment" \ | jq '{text, words: (.words | length), segments: (.segments | length)}' { "text": "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. Light LLM keeps every timestamp granularity.", "words": 15, "segments": 2 } ``` 2. signals.title: test(e2e): record and replay the non-streaming provider flows
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Record mode wrote no bundle for the non-streaming flows - Replay dialed the real providers instead of the recording - Multipart uploads re-keyed every run, so they always missed How it solves it: - Four non-streaming suites now register through the provider edge - Uploads key on parsed fields and file content, not the envelope - Binary uploads hash byte for byte instead of a lossy decode ## User Flow **Before**: recording the non-streaming flows produces no bundle at all, and replaying them dials the real providers and fails on credentials. 1. Engineer starts a gateway on `http://127.0.0.1:41847` with real `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, and confirms `GET http://127.0.0.1:41847/health/liveliness` returns 200 2. Runs the four non-streaming tests in record mode with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record E2E_FIXTURE_DIR=/tmp/e2e-fixtures`, covering chat completions, embeddings, `POST /v1/messages`, and an OpenAI batch file upload. Sees `4 passed in 65s`, and every one of them billed the real providers 3. Opens `/tmp/e2e-fixtures` expecting the recording, and finds the directory was never created. No manifest, no per-test folders, and nothing in the run output said a single call went unrecorded 4. Restarts the gateway with bogus keys and re-runs the same four tests with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=replay` against that directory. Collection aborts before any test runs: `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=replay cannot use bundle at /tmp/e2e-fixtures: no manifest.json found` 5. Points replay at a bundle recorded earlier from the one already-wired suite, so collection gets past the gate. All four tests now fail with `401 Incorrect API key provided: sk-bogus****alid` from OpenAI and Anthropic, because the gateway dialed the providers directly no matter what the fixture mode said 6. Tries the batch file upload on its own against the edge. Every run computes a different key for the same upload, since the digest is taken over the raw multipart body and its boundary is regenerated per request, so it always comes back `599` with no recorded match **After**: the same commands record a real bundle and replay it offline, with bogus credentials proving no provider was reached. 1. Engineer starts a gateway on `http://127.0.0.1:41847` with real `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, and confirms `GET http://127.0.0.1:41847/health/liveliness` returns 200 2. Runs the four non-streaming tests in record mode with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record E2E_FIXTURE_DIR=/tmp/e2e-fixtures`, covering chat completions, embeddings, `POST /v1/messages`, and an OpenAI batch file upload. Sees `4 passed in 65s`, and every one of them billed the real providers 3. Opens `/tmp/e2e-fixtures` and finds `manifest.json` plus one folder per test holding six recorded calls in call order, including `0000-post-openai-v1-files.json` for the upload and the `GET` and `DELETE` that follow it. Each stored call shows `"headers": {}`, so neither API key is written anywhere 4. Restarts the gateway with bogus keys and re-runs the same four tests with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=replay` against that directory. Sees `4 passed in 61s`, spending nothing and making no provider call 5. Re-runs those same four tests against that same bogus-key gateway with the fixture mode unset, and watches them fail with `401 Incorrect API key provided: sk-bogus****alid`, which is what confirms the passing replay run was answered from the recording 6. Re-runs the batch file upload on its own as often as they like. Each run builds a fresh multipart boundary and still matches the recording, because the upload is keyed on its `purpose` field and the name, digest, and length of the file part rather than on the envelope around them ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5974 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup for every case below: a gateway on `http://127.0.0.1:41847` against local Postgres, started once with real provider keys and once with `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-bogus-lit5974-never-valid` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-bogus-lit5974-never-valid`. The four node ids under test, run from `tests/e2e`: ``` llm_translation/test_chat_completions_contract_e2e.py::TestChatCompletionsContract::test_success_response_matches_chat_completion_contract llm_translation/test_embeddings_endpoint_e2e.py::TestEmbeddingsEndpoint::test_embeddings_returns_vector llm_translation/test_messages_e2e.py::TestAnthropicMessages::test_messages_returns_completion batches/test_batches_e2e.py::TestBatchFileContent::test_file_content_matches_upload ``` ### Before (7cb100af63) Run in its own worktree at the merge base, on its own gateway and its own database, so nothing here shares state with the After run. #### Replay reaches the provider instead of the bundle This is the leg that pairs with the After run below: the same four node ids, the same bundle, the same bogus keys, and the only difference is the commit the gateway booted from. 1. Gateway restarted with the bogus keys, and the bundle recorded above copied in untouched 2. `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=replay E2E_FIXTURE_DIR=$BUNDLE_COPY python -m pytest <the same four node ids> -v` 3. Collection reads the bundle and accepts it, so nothing was refused for format, manifest, or age: ``` e2e fixture mode: replay <- .../bundle-copy (recorded 2026-08-22T01:46:12.680889+00:00, harness 7cb100af63) ``` 4. `4 failed in 61.76s (0:01:01)`, every one of them a live provider rejection rather than a replay miss: ``` chat completions: litellm.AuthenticationError: OpenAIException - Incorrect API key provided: sk-bogus****************alid embeddings: litellm.AuthenticationError: OpenAIException - Error code: 401 - Incorrect API key provided: sk-bogus****************alid messages: {"type":"error","error":{"type":"authentication_error","message":"API key is invalid."}} batches upload: AssertionError: kind='unauthorized' ... 'Incorrect API key provided: sk-bogus****************alid' ``` The bundle was readable and in date; the four tests just never consulted it. #### Record mode passes while writing nothing 1. `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record E2E_FIXTURE_DIR=$CASE1 python -m pytest <the same four node ids> -v`, with the banner confirming `e2e fixture mode: record -> .../case1-fixtures` 2. `4 passed in 63.90s (0:01:03)`, all four billed against real OpenAI and Anthropic 3. `ls -la $CASE1` reports `No such file or directory` So record mode is not merely lossy at the merge base, it is silent: the run passes, spends real money, and leaves nothing on disk to replay from. #### Why, at the merge base 1. None of the four suites is edge-wired. `provider_edge_base` has exactly one caller in the tree, `quota_management/spend_tracking/test_provider_edge_spend_e2e.py`, and all four tests register their deployment with only `model=` and `api_key=`, no `api_base`. `provider_edge.py` says as much itself: "suites that do not wire the edge keep hitting providers live in every mode" 2. Multipart identity is boundary-contaminated. Calling the merge-base `_edge_request` directly on two uploads that differ only in their generated boundary gives two different keys, and even the byte count moves: ``` record-run key: post /openai/v1/files #0c49d65e18ab863f replay-run key: post /openai/v1/files #fe8cb47e8e23b09e keys match : False a: form=None file_name=None file_bytes=297 b: form=None file_name=None file_bytes=300 ``` Contrast that with the recording the PR produces, which carries `form`, `file_name`, `file_sha256`, and a stable `file_bytes`. A third case confirms no 599 is even reachable at the merge base: recording the upload alone writes no bundle, so replaying it aborts at collection with `no manifest.json found` rather than missing against a recording. ### After (d4162bd1ca) #### Record with real credentials writes the bundle 1. `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record E2E_FIXTURE_DIR=$BUNDLE python -m pytest <the four node ids> -v` 2. `4 passed in 65.85s (0:01:05)` 3. `find $BUNDLE -type f` lists `manifest.json` and six recorded calls across four per-test folders, including `test_file_content_matches_upload-9f2f8f11/0000-post-openai-v1-files.json` plus the `GET` and `DELETE` that follow it 4. The recorded upload keys on what it says, with no credentials on disk: ```json { "method": "post", "path": "/openai/v1/files", "headers": {}, "form": {"purpose": "batch"}, "file_name": "file:modified_file.jsonl", "file_sha256": "b2c7242400c2625612f455966aabe191e218420a120450eeb05d4d3b16016d61", "file_bytes": 173 } ``` #### Replay with bogus credentials passes offline 1. Gateway restarted with the bogus keys above 2. `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=replay E2E_FIXTURE_DIR=$BUNDLE python -m pytest <the same four node ids> -v` 3. `4 passed in 60.92s (0:01:00)`, with the upload matching across a freshly generated multipart boundary #### Control: the same bogus gateway fails the moment the edge is out of the loop 1. Gateway still running with the bogus keys, fixture mode unset 2. `python -m pytest <the chat completions and batches node ids> -v` 3. `2 failed in 31.33s`, both with `AssertionError: kind='unauthorized'` carrying `Error code: 401 ... 'Incorrect API key provided: sk-bogus****************alid'` 4. This is what makes the replay run above proof: the credentials really were bogus, so the passing replay was answered from the bundle rather than by OpenAI #### Offline coverage of the multipart keying 1. `python -m pytest tests/e2e/test_provider_edge.py -q` 2. `31 passed in 26.77s`, including the five added cases: a fresh boundary replays the same upload, the stored request carries fields and file identity but no secrets, a structurally different upload misses, several file parts separate when their contents swap, and a body that contradicts its declared boundary stays opaque 3. `make check` reports `check: PASS` with `0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes` from basedpyright over `tests/e2e` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) - Streaming `/v1/messages` stays live; fidelity is LIT-5742 - Bundles are never committed; CI publishing is LIT-5748 - Batches replay needs a database without the record run's rows - Uploads routed by `files_settings` pass no deployment, so stay live - Bedrock cannot be mounted, since SigV4 signs the Host header ## QA runbook Prerequisites for every checklist below: a live proxy with `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set, `LITELLM_PROXY_URL` and `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` exported for pytest, and `DATABASE_URL` pointing at a Postgres the run may write to. Every replay step wants the proxy restarted with deliberately invalid provider keys, since that is what proves no provider was reached. - tests/e2e/test_provider_edge.py::TestMultipartIdentity::test_a_fresh_boundary_replays_the_same_upload - the same upload recorded once replays on a later run whose multipart boundary is different - [ ] Record the upload flow: `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record E2E_FIXTURE_DIR=/tmp/qa-5974 uv run pytest tests/e2e/batches/test_batches_e2e.py::TestBatchFileContent::test_file_content_matches_upload` - [ ] Confirm `/tmp/qa-5974/*/0000-post-openai-v1-files.json` exists and its `file_sha256` is a digest while `headers` is `{}` - [ ] Restart the proxy with an invalid `OPENAI_API_KEY`, then replay the same node id with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=replay E2E_FIXTURE_DIR=/tmp/qa-5974` - [ ] Expect it to pass, and expect a repeat replay to pass again even though httpx built a new boundary each time - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey or potentially flaky - tests/e2e/test_provider_edge.py::TestMultipartIdentity::test_the_stored_request_carries_fields_and_file_identity_but_no_secrets - a recorded upload keeps its form fields and file identity while no credential reaches disk - [ ] With the bundle from the previous checklist, open the recorded `POST /v1/files` file - [ ] Expect `"headers": {}` and `"form": {"purpose": "batch"}`, a `file_name` of `field:filename` shape, plus `file_sha256` and `file_bytes` - [ ] Grep the whole bundle for your key prefix (`grep -r "sk-" /tmp/qa-5974`) and expect no match - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey or potentially flaky - tests/e2e/test_provider_edge.py::TestMultipartIdentity::test_a_structurally_different_upload_misses - an upload whose content really changed fails loudly instead of matching the old recording - [ ] Record the upload flow as above, then edit the JSONL payload the test uploads so its content differs - [ ] Replay that node id against the untouched bundle - [ ] Expect an HTTP 599 naming the computed key and the closest recorded key, never a silent pass and never a live call - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey or potentially flaky - tests/e2e/test_provider_edge.py::TestMultipartIdentity::test_several_file_parts_separate_when_their_contents_swap - two file parts in one upload stay distinguishable when their contents trade places - [ ] Send a two-file multipart upload through an edge-wired deployment in record mode - [ ] Replay the same request with the two file contents swapped between the parts - [ ] Expect a 599 miss rather than a match, since each part's identity carries its own field name and digest - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey or potentially flaky - tests/e2e/test_provider_edge.py::TestMultipartIdentity::test_a_body_that_does_not_match_its_declared_boundary_stays_opaque - a body that contradicts its own content-type still keys stably instead of randomly - [ ] Send a request whose `Content-Type` declares a multipart boundary the body never uses, in record mode - [ ] Replay the identical request and expect it to match - [ ] Confirm the recorded call carries `file_name` of `<unparsed-multipart>`, which is what says the envelope did not parse - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey or potentially flaky - tests/e2e/llm_translation/test_chat_completions_contract_e2e.py, test_embeddings_endpoint_e2e.py, test_messages_e2e.py, and batches/test_batches_e2e.py - the four wired suites record and replay, and are unchanged when no fixture mode is set - [ ] Run all four node ids from the Proof of Fix section with no `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE` at all and expect them to pass against the live providers exactly as before - [ ] Re-run them with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record E2E_FIXTURE_DIR=/tmp/qa-5974-all` and expect a bundle holding one folder per test - [ ] Restart the proxy with invalid provider keys and replay that bundle, expecting all four to pass - [ ] Re-run those same four with the fixture mode unset against the invalid-key proxy and expect 401s, which is the control that the replay pass was real - [ ] Sanity check: these tests make sense to change and are not hand-wavey or potentially flaky ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(complexity-router): retune default tier boundaries to 0.10 / 0.25 / 0.50
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Stock boundaries park technical, multi-part prompts in cheap tiers - Scorer rarely clears 0.35, so COMPLEX is nearly unreachable - Overriding one boundary silently left the other two stale How it solves it: - Retunes shipped defaults to 0.10 / 0.25 / 0.50 - Labelled eval accuracy goes from 28/29 to 29/29 - Missing boundaries now fill from the one canonical default ## User Flow Before: a developer sending a detailed engineering question to an auto router gets the cheapest model back, and the answer is thinner than the question deserves 1. Their admin configures an auto router named `smart-router` with four tiers and no custom score boundaries 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "smart-router"` and ask a multi-part networking question spanning use cases, performance, and packet loss 3. The reply comes back from the cheapest tier model, visible as `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` in the `x-litellm-model-name` response header 4. They send a second request asking for a distributed rate limiter in Python backed by Redis, and it comes back from the second-cheapest tier 5. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and see both requests billed against the bottom two tiers, so they stop trusting the router and pin a model by hand After: the same two requests reach models that match the question 1. Their admin configures the same auto router, still with no custom score boundaries 2. They send the same multi-part networking question to `"model": "smart-router"` 3. The reply now comes from the mid tier, `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` in `x-litellm-model-name` 4. The rate limiter request now comes from the tier above that, `claude-sonnet-4-6` 5. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows both at the tier the prompt warranted, and an admin who preferred the old split can set `tier_boundaries` back to 0.15 / 0.35 / 0.60 ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, identical on both sides. The auto router deliberately sets no `tier_boundaries`, so it runs on whatever the build ships, and each tier points at a real model through a live gateway ```yaml model_list: - model_name: tier-simple litellm_params: model: openai/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 api_base: https://gateway.litellm-sandbox.ai/v1 api_key: os.environ/GW_KEY - model_name: tier-medium litellm_params: model: openai/claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 api_base: https://gateway.litellm-sandbox.ai/v1 api_key: os.environ/GW_KEY - model_name: tier-complex litellm_params: model: openai/claude-sonnet-4-6 api_base: https://gateway.litellm-sandbox.ai/v1 api_key: os.environ/GW_KEY - model_name: tier-reasoning litellm_params: model: openai/claude-sonnet-5 api_base: https://gateway.litellm-sandbox.ai/v1 api_key: os.environ/GW_KEY - model_name: smart-router litellm_params: model: auto_router/complexity_router complexity_router_config: tiers: SIMPLE: tier-simple MEDIUM: tier-medium COMPLEX: tier-complex REASONING: tier-reasoning general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` Both runs boot the proxy the same way, then read back the tier that actually served each request ```bash python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config boundaries_proof.yaml --port 4055 curl -s http://localhost:4055/public/complexity_router/scorer_defaults curl -s -D - -o /dev/null http://localhost:4055/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' \ -d '{"model":"smart-router","max_tokens":16,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<prompt>"}]}' \ | grep -i 'x-litellm-model-name\|x-litellm-response-cost' ``` ### Before (76d46274c1) #### Shipped boundaries 1. `curl -s http://localhost:4055/public/complexity_router/scorer_defaults` 2. `{'simple_medium': 0.15, 'medium_complex': 0.35, 'complex_reasoning': 0.6}` #### Multi-part networking question 1. Prompt: "Explain the differences between TCP and UDP protocols, including use cases for each, performance implications, and how they handle packet loss in distributed systems" 2. `x-litellm-model-name: openai/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.000115`, so it lands on SIMPLE #### Distributed rate limiter 1. Prompt: "Implement a rate limiter using the token bucket algorithm in Python that supports multiple rate limit tiers and can be used across distributed systems with Redis as the backend" 2. `x-litellm-model-name: openai/claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929`, `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.000357`, so it lands on MEDIUM ### After (3b39ebc093) #### Shipped boundaries 1. `curl -s http://localhost:4055/public/complexity_router/scorer_defaults` 2. `{'simple_medium': 0.1, 'medium_complex': 0.25, 'complex_reasoning': 0.5}` #### Multi-part networking question 1. Same prompt as above 2. `x-litellm-model-name: openai/claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929`, `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.000345`, so it now lands on MEDIUM #### Distributed rate limiter 1. Same prompt as above 2. `x-litellm-model-name: openai/claude-sonnet-4-6`, `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.000357`, so it now lands on COMPLEX Both prompts are labelled COMPLEX in the in-repo eval set, so each moves toward its label. Across that whole set the retune moves 5 of 29 cases up a tier and takes accuracy from 28/29 to 29/29 ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Higher tiers cost more; deployments watching spend should re-baseline - `reasoning_override_min_score` tracks `simple_medium`, so its floor drops too - Labelled eval set is only 29 cases - Old behaviour is one `tier_boundaries` block away ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(websearch_interception): end the turn when the agentic loop hits its ceiling
signals.text: ## TLDR When the web search interception loop hits its ceiling, `/v1/messages` now ends the turn cleanly instead of handing the client a `tool_use` block for `litellm_web_search`, an internal tool the client never declared and has no way to answer. Also adds a `max_agentic_loops` setting to `websearch_interception_params` ## User Flow **Before** The turn comes back carrying a tool call the app never asked for, so it has nothing to answer with and the conversation dead-ends. 1. A developer runs a LiteLLM proxy with web search interception turned on for their Bedrock Claude models, pointed at their search provider. They try to raise the search loop's ceiling with `max_agentic_loops: 5` under `litellm_settings.websearch_interception_params`; the proxy starts fine and the key does nothing, so the ceiling stays at the default of 3 unless they repeat it under every model's `litellm_params` 2. From an internal research app built on Anthropic's Python SDK (`client.messages.create`, no streaming) and pointed at the proxy, they ask a question that needs several rounds of searching, something like "compare current on-demand H100 pricing at the three biggest cloud providers and tell me which is cheapest" 3. The app sends `POST https://litellm-proxy/v1/messages` with `"model": "claude-sonnet-4-5"`, no `stream`, and `"tools": [{"type": "web_search_20250305", "name": "web_search"}]` 4. The proxy runs the searches on their behalf and asks the model again after each round, up to 3 rounds 5. The model asks for one more search after the last allowed round 6. `HTTP 200` comes back with `"stop_reason": "tool_use"` and a content block `{"type": "tool_use", "id": "toolu_01...", "name": "litellm_web_search", "input": {"query": "..."}}` 7. The app has no tool by that name. It declared Anthropic's `web_search` and nothing else, so there is nothing to run and no result to hand back, and the person waiting on the answer gets none 8. The developer appends that assistant turn and sends the next `POST https://litellm-proxy/v1/messages` anyway, and gets `HTTP 400` because the `tool_use` block has no matching `tool_result`. The only way forward is to throw the turn away and start the conversation over **After** The turn comes back finished, the app renders the answer, and the next message goes through. 1. Same setup, except `max_agentic_loops: 5` under `litellm_settings.websearch_interception_params` now applies to every intercepted model, and a value the loop cannot honor (`0`, `-1`, `"five"`, `true`) stops the proxy at startup with a message naming the key instead of being quietly ignored. A per model `litellm_params.max_agentic_loops` still wins where it is set 2. The same question from the same app 3. The same `POST https://litellm-proxy/v1/messages` request 4. The proxy runs the searches on their behalf and asks the model again after each round, up to the ceiling 5. The model asks for one more search after the last allowed round 6. `HTTP 200` comes back with `"stop_reason": "end_turn"`, the text and web search result blocks the turn produced, and no block named `litellm_web_search` anywhere in the body 7. The app renders the answer. It can be thinner than it would have been with more rounds, since the searching stopped at the ceiling, and `max_agentic_loops` is the knob for that 8. The developer sends their follow-up `POST https://litellm-proxy/v1/messages` with that assistant turn in the history and gets `HTTP 200`. The conversation carries on ## What was happening `_check_agentic_loop_safety` raised a `ValueError` when the loop ceiling or the repeated tool-call fingerprint guard tripped. That raise crossed the parent frame's unguarded `await anthropic_messages.acreate(...)` in `_execute_anthropic_agentic_plan`, so the parent's `async_post_agentic_loop_response_hook` never ran, and one frame further up an `except Exception` swallowed it and logged `LiteLLM.AgenticHookError`. The response that then fell through to the client was the raw model turn, internal `tool_use` block and all ## The fix `_check_agentic_loop_safety` now raises `AgenticLoopSafetyError`, which subclasses `ValueError` so anything already catching the broader type keeps working. `_call_agentic_completion_hooks` catches that specific type and returns a finalized response: the blocks for the tool calls the rail just refused are dropped, and if nothing the client declared is left waiting, `stop_reason` is closed out. It returns through `_maybe_wrap_in_fake_stream` like every other path there, so a converted stream still gets a stream back. The refused blocks are matched by the ids and names of the tool calls the safety check refused rather than by hardcoding `litellm_web_search`, since this machinery is not web search specific. A block that carries an id is matched on the id alone, so a tool the client declared under the same name as a refused one is left alone The terminal response only replaces the turn on the non-streaming `/v1/messages` path, which is where the bug was reported and which includes a streaming client whose request the interceptor converted. The two other callers keep raising exactly as they do today. A genuinely streaming caller has already sent the original message to the client by the time the hooks run, so a finalized turn would arrive as a second `message_start` through `message_stop` rather than replace the first one, and I measured that duplicate before scoping it. The responses surface hands this code a pydantic model rather than the Anthropic dict the finalizer rewrites, so returning it would turn a loud failure into a quiet 200 that still carries the internal call. Both are worth fixing and neither is fixable here One decision worth pushing back on if you disagree: the terminal `stop_reason` is `end_turn`. The type at `litellm/types/llms/anthropic_messages/anthropic_response.py` is `Literal["end_turn", "max_tokens", "stop_sequence", "tool_use"] | None`, so there is no truncation value to use, and inventing a new string breaks the type and strict SDK clients. `end_turn` is also what the real Anthropic API returns for the same question when its own server side web search stops calling tools. `max_tokens` was the alternative and it would be a lie: nothing hit a token limit, and clients that auto-continue on `max_tokens` would start a pointless follow-up turn ## The knob `max_agentic_loops` is now readable from `litellm_settings.websearch_interception_params`, so the ceiling can be set for the feature as a whole. The interceptor injects it from its pre-request hook, which runs on `/v1/messages`, so that is the surface it covers. The per deployment setting below is the one that applies wherever the loop runs: ```yaml litellm_settings: callbacks: ["websearch_interception"] websearch_interception_params: enabled_providers: ["bedrock"] search_tool_name: "my-tavily-search" max_agentic_loops: 5 ``` To be clear about what this adds: a per deployment `litellm_params.max_agentic_loops` already worked before this PR and still wins over the feature-level setting, so this is a convenience for operators who want one ceiling for every intercepted model rather than a new capability. `max_agentic_loops` stays on the proxy's untrusted root field list, so a client still cannot raise its own ceiling from the request body A value that the loop cannot honor (zero, negative, a string, a bool) is rejected when the config is read rather than quietly ignored. That is stricter than the rest of this handler, which tends to coerce and fall back, so it is easy to soften if reviewers prefer. It can only fire on a config that sets the new key ## Not in this PR - The chat completions sibling loop in `litellm/litellm_core_utils/chat_completion_agentic_loop.py` leaks the same way. PR #37657 is editing that file right now, so it is a follow-up rather than a conflict - A genuinely streaming request, meaning one the interceptor did not convert, still leaks the internal `tool_use` block, because the message is on the wire before the cap is even checked. Ending that turn cleanly means catching the rail before the first message is sent rather than after, which is a bigger change to the streaming iterator than this fix should carry - The responses surface still returns a 500 when a rail trips. Giving it the same treatment means teaching the finalizer the responses shape, which is worth doing on its own rather than inside a `/v1/messages` fix - When the refused block was the only thing in the turn, the client gets `end_turn` with empty content instead of text saying the search was cut short. That is recoverable where the old behavior was not, but it is thin, and writing assistant text on the model's behalf felt like a product call rather than a bug fix - On a multi hop search, only the outermost loop injects the native `server_tool_use` and `web_search_tool_result` blocks, because the follow-up kwargs strip the flag that turns them on. This fix restores the post-loop hook run on the frame that was being skipped, but it does not make every executed search show up in the response. That gap is being tracked separately - The fake Anthropic stream iterator only emits `content_block_start` for `text`, `thinking`, `redacted_thinking` and `tool_use`, while it emits `content_block_stop` for every block, so `server_tool_use` and `web_search_tool_result` come out as an orphan stop with no start. That is tracked separately, and it matters here: on a capped streaming turn the internal tool call is now gone and those two blocks are the only ones left, so the client sees a terminal stream with no content in it. The turn is at least terminal and recoverable, where before it was neither, but the streaming client still gets less than the non-streaming one until that iterator is fixed. The blocks themselves do survive the cap, which is what the orphan stops at index 0 and 1 show, so this is presentation and not data loss - The capped streaming path is not cost attributed, while the identical non-streaming request is, also tracked separately - The Anthropic agentic path never runs `_run_agentic_loop_cleanup`, where the Responses path does. That is pre-existing and not specific to the ceiling, so changing it would move behavior for every intercepted anthropic request ## Testing New unit tests in `tests/test_litellm/integrations/websearch_interception/test_websearch_agentic_loop_cap.py` cover the capped response being terminal, the same for the repeated fingerprint guard, no follow-up call being planned once a rail trips, the caller's response not being mutated, a client declared `tool_use` surviving with `stop_reason` left alone, only the refused tool calls being dropped when a client declares a tool of the same name, tool calls without ids still matching by name, a non-dict response passing through untouched, the converted stream still getting a terminal fake stream, the streaming and responses callers still raising, the parent frame's post-loop hook running and its blocks landing, and the new knob from config through to the loop settings including precedence and rejected values Verified live as well, on a proxy against the real Anthropic API with a real search backend and `max_agentic_loops: 2` set through the new setting, using a prompt that forces one search per turn so the loop actually chains. The proxy logged `LiteLLM.AgenticLoopRefused: ending turn ... Exceeded max_agentic_loops=2` once per capped request and no `AgenticHookError` at all, where before the fix that same request logged `AgenticHookError`. It returned: - non-streaming: HTTP 200, `stop_reason: end_turn`, blocks `['server_tool_use', 'web_search_tool_result']`, no `tool_use` block, and the string `litellm_web_search` nowhere in the body. On the same request before the fix: blocks `['server_tool_use', 'web_search_tool_result', 'text', 'tool_use']` with `stop_reason: tool_use` and the internal tool name in the body - streaming: HTTP 200, `stop_reason: end_turn` in `message_delta`, clean `message_stop`, no `content_block_start` naming the internal tool - below the ceiling: unchanged, one search, `end_turn`, citations present, and a correct answer

signals.text: ## Verify Docker Image Signature All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0). **Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):** A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key: ```bash cosign verify \ --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \ ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.99.0-dev.2 ``` **Verify using the release tag (convenience):** Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules: ```bash cosign verify \ --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.99.0-dev.2/cosign.pub \ ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.99.0-dev.2 ``` Expected output: ``` The following checks were performed on each of these signatures: - The cosign claims were validated - The signatures were verified signal.title: fix(ptu): warn when config.yaml declares PTU while attribution is off
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - PTU in config.yaml accrues nothing while the feature is off - Nothing anywhere says so, so operators assume it is on - A typo drops the deployment with no hint which feature it was How it solves it: - Registration names the declaring deployments once, at startup - The line points at the env var that turns attribution on - Behavior is unchanged: nothing is stripped, rejected, or rescued ## User Flow Before: an admin reserves Azure PTU capacity in config.yaml, and their team's spend never reflects it 1. They add `ptu_count`, `cost_per_ptu_per_hour`, `ptu_effective_from` and `team_id` to a deployment in config.yaml 2. They restart the proxy, which starts cleanly and logs nothing about the reservation 3. They send traffic to that model and it answers normally 4. Days later they open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=usage, filter to the team, and see only per-token spend; the hourly reservation they configured is nowhere 5. Nothing in the startup log, the model page, or the usage page ever mentioned that the feature was switched off After: the same restart tells them the feature is off and names the variable that turns it on 1. They add the same fields to the same deployment in config.yaml 2. They restart the proxy and the startup log says PTU fields are set on `azure-ptu`, that attribution is disabled so no flat cost accrues and the traffic bills per token, and that `LITELLM_ENABLE_PTU_COST_ATTRIBUTION=True` enables it 3. They set that variable and restart; the line is gone 4. They send traffic, and https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=usage now shows the reservation's hourly cost against the team ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Refs LIT-5809 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, both sides. A real Gemini deployment carrying a reservation, alongside an ordinary one, with `LITELLM_ENABLE_PTU_COST_ATTRIBUTION` unset: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gemini-ptu litellm_params: model: gemini/gemini-2.5-flash api_key: os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY model_info: id: gemini-ptu-eastus team_id: team-alpha ptu_count: 100 cost_per_ptu_per_hour: 0.02 ptu_effective_from: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" - model_name: gemini-ondemand litellm_params: model: gemini/gemini-2.5-flash api_key: os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY ``` The typo case reuses the same file with `ptu_count: 0`. Both sides run against the same Postgres, launched with `python -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli --config <file>` ### Before (4e19127350) #### A reservation declared while attribution is off 1. Start the proxy on the config above, then read the startup log for anything naming PTU: ``` $ grep -ci "PTU cost attribution is disabled" base_valid.log 0 $ grep -i "ptu" base_valid.log | grep -v register_model gemini-ptu ``` 2. The only mention is the deployment's own name in the model list. Nothing says the feature is off 3. The deployment registers and serves: ``` $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4892/model/info -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." | jq -r '.data[] | "\(.model_name) | ptu_count=\(.model_info.ptu_count)"' gemini-ptu | ptu_count=100 gemini-ondemand | ptu_count=null ``` #### A typo in the same reservation 1. Restart on the same file with `ptu_count: 0`, then read the log: ``` $ grep -ci "PTU cost attribution is disabled" base_typo.log 0 $ grep "Error creating deployment" base_typo.log | head -1 19:17:57 - LiteLLM Router:ERROR: router.py:7797 - Error creating deployment: 1 validation error for ModelInfo ``` 2. The deployment is gone, and the error names a pydantic model rather than the feature: ``` $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4892/model/info -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." | jq -r '[.data[].model_name]' ["gemini-ondemand"] ``` ### After (08ca52e846) #### A reservation declared while attribution is off 1. Start the proxy on the same config. The startup log now says so, once: ``` $ grep -c "PTU cost attribution is disabled" flagoff.log 1 $ grep "PTU cost attribution" flagoff.log 19:13:18 - LiteLLM Router:WARNING: router.py:8247 - PTU fields are set on config.yaml deployment(s) gemini-ptu, but PTU cost attribution is disabled, so no flat cost accrues and this traffic is billed per token. Set LITELLM_ENABLE_PTU_COST_ATTRIBUTION=True to enable it ``` 2. Only the declaring deployment is named; `gemini-ondemand` is not 3. The deployment registers and serves exactly as before: ``` $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4891/model/info -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." | jq -r '.data[] | "\(.model_name) | id=\(.model_info.id)"' gemini-ptu | id=gemini-ptu-eastus gemini-ondemand | id=76058c439c2182aa7c8fd6a55729eb958321073699bf718f5cc5f7a34bf0d8af ``` 4. A real call through it, on a team key, confirms the line's claim about per-token billing: ``` $ curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4891/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-<team key>" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"gemini-ptu","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with the single word: reserved"}]}' reply: reserved usage: {'completion_tokens': 27, 'prompt_tokens': 8, 'total_tokens': 35} ``` ``` $ psql -tAc "select model_group, spend, ptu_flat_cost is not null from ..." gemini-ptu|6.99e-05 <- billed per token team-alpha|6.99e-05|0 <- LiteLLM_DailyTeamSpend: no flat cost accrued ``` #### The feature switched on 1. Restart with `LITELLM_ENABLE_PTU_COST_ATTRIBUTION=True` on the same config: ``` $ grep -c "PTU cost attribution is disabled" flagon.log 0 $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4891/model/info -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." | jq -r '.data[] | "\(.model_name) | ptu_count=\(.model_info.ptu_count)"' gemini-ptu | ptu_count=100 gemini-ondemand | ptu_count=null ``` 2. The line is gone and the deployment is unchanged #### A typo in the same reservation 1. Restart on the `ptu_count: 0` file with attribution still off. Both lines now appear together: ``` $ grep -E "PTU cost attribution is disabled|Error creating deployment" typo.log 19:14:17 - LiteLLM Router:WARNING: router.py:8247 - PTU fields are set on config.yaml deployment(s) gemini-ptu, but PTU cost attribution is disabled, ... 19:14:17 - LiteLLM Router:ERROR: router.py:7799 - Error creating deployment: 1 validation error for ModelInfo ``` 2. The deployment is still dropped, unchanged from base; what is new is that the operator can see which feature the vanished entry belonged to: ``` $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4891/model/info -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." | jq -r '[.data[].model_name]' ["gemini-ondemand"] ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - The typo still drops the deployment; only the silence is fixed - Fires once per Router build, so once per boot or reload - The flag is read only when a config deployment declares PTU ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > Logging-only change on router registration; no billing, auth, or deployment-acceptance behavior is modified. > > **Overview** > Warns at router startup when `config.yaml` deployments set PTU fields while `LITELLM_ENABLE_PTU_COST_ATTRIBUTION` is off, so operators are not left thinking reserved capacity is accruing when traffic is still billed per token. > > Adds `declares_ptu` and logs one warning naming every non-`db_model` declaring deployment (including incomplete or invalid PTU values).
