signal.text: ## Relevant issues Fixes #28409 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Original report (#28409, hit in production on v1.83.14 with real PDF document-understanding traffic): `trim_messages` on a valid payload from https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/completion/document_understanding raised ``` ValueError: Invalid content item type: file. Expected str or dict with 'type' field (text, image_url, tool_use, tool_result, thinking). ``` **The failure mode has since gotten quieter but not better**: on base `10d5804b3e`, `trim_messages` now swallows the token_counter error and silently returns the conversation **untrimmed** — over-budget conversations containing a file block are never trimmed, with no error to notice. Before (base `10d5804b3e`): ``` $ pytest tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_token_counter.py -k file_content_block -q FAILED ...::test_token_counter_with_file_content_block - ValueError: Invalid content item type: file FAILED ...::test_trim_messages_with_file_content_block - trim_messages must actually trim an over-budget conversation containing a file content block — got 3 messages back (input 3) 2 failed ``` After (this PR, `feda8c722e`): ``` $ pytest tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_token_counter.py -q 89 passed, 1 skipped ``` (new tests: token_counter returns a positive count for a file block; the opaque base64 `file_data` blob does not change the count — verified small vs 100KB blob count identical; a bare `file_data`-only block doesn't raise; `trim_messages` actually trims an over-budget conversation containing a file block.) `ruff format --check` / `ruff check` pass on the touched file. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes - `_count_content_list`: handle `{"type": "file", "file": {...}}` (OpenAI document understanding / `ChatCompletionFileObject`). The real token cost is the provider's server-side document extraction and can't be derived client-side, and counting the base64 `file_data` blob would wildly overcount — so count only the lightweight textual fields (`file_id`, `filename`, `format`), mirroring how `tool_reference` blocks count just the tool name. - Add `file` to the supported-types enumeration in the catch-all error message. - 2 tests, both failing on base. <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches token counting and proxy budget reservation, which affect trimming and spend admission. File uploads now over-reserve at max_input_tokens rather than undercounting document extraction. > > **Overview** > Fixes #28409: `token_counter` / `trim_messages` no longer fail or skip trimming on OpenAI document-understanding payloads (`{"type": "file", ...}`). > > `_count_content_list` now treats `file` like other known block types. Only lightweight fields (`file_id`, `filename`, `format`) are counted; opaque `file_data` is ignored so base64 blobs cannot inflate the count. Real document tokens are provider-side and cannot be estimated client-side. > > Budget reservation skips that undercount: if messages contain a `file` block, `_estimate_input_tokens` falls through to `max_input_tokens` instead of reserving from filename/id only. Plain text requests still use normal counting. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 7b28fbfdfcfc4921bab1caa8e95bb1f653e70b27. signal.title: fix(cost): honour deployment custom pricing for OCR calls
signal.text: ## Title fix(cost): honour deployment custom pricing for OCR calls ## Relevant issues Fixes #36608 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have Added testing in the `tests/litellm/` directory - [x] I have added a screenshot of my new test passing locally - [x] My PR passes all unit tests - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `ocr_cost()` resolved pricing only through `litellm.get_model_info()` — a cost map lookup keyed by model name. Custom pricing for a router deployment is registered under the **deployment id**, and `_register_custom_pricing_for_request()` deliberately strips pricing fields from the shared `{provider}/{model}` key so siblings don't clobber each other. So the key `ocr_cost()` looked up was exactly the one guaranteed not to carry the pricing. Result: an OCR model absent from the cost map billed **$0** regardless of configuration, even though `ocr_cost_per_page` / `ocr_cost_per_credit` are declared `CustomPricingLiteLLMParams` fields and are accepted without error. This mirrors the existing **video generation** path rather than inventing a mechanism. That path already had the same problem — pricing that isn't token-based can't travel via `custom_cost_per_token` — and solves it by pulling deployment `model_info` off the logging object: ```python if custom_pricing and litellm_logging_obj is not None: _litellm_params = getattr(litellm_logging_obj, "litellm_params", None) if _litellm_params is not None: _metadata = _litellm_params.get("metadata", {}) or {} _video_model_info = _metadata.get("model_info", None) ``` So: - `ocr_cost()` takes an optional `model_info` and prefers it over the map **only when it actually carries OCR pricing**; otherwise the existing map lookup runs unchanged. - `cost_per_token()` gains an optional `custom_model_info` passthrough. - `completion_cost()` extracts it the same way the video branch does. Backwards compatible — every new parameter defaults to `None`, and with nothing configured the behaviour is byte-for-byte what it was, including still returning `0.0` for a genuinely unpriced model. ## Testing New file `tests/test_litellm/test_ocr_custom_pricing.py`, 8 tests. **6 of them fail on the base branch and pass with this change**; the other 2 are controls that must pass either way (the premise guard that the test model really is absent from the map, and the unchanged-$0 behaviour when nothing is configured). ``` $ pytest tests/test_litellm/test_ocr_custom_pricing.py -q ........ [100%] 8 passed in 0.29s # with the fix reverted: 6 failed, 2 passed in 0.45s ``` Wider cost suite, no regressions (`test_cost_calculator.py`, `test_gpt_image_cost_calculator.py`, `test_register_model_zero_cost_persistence.py`, `test_router_model_cost_isolation.py`): ``` 1 failed, 133 passed ``` The single failure is `test_router_model_cost_isolation.py::test_custom_pricing_isolated_from_sibling_via_proxy_model_info_path`, which fails **identically on a clean checkout** of this base branch — a `ModuleNotFoundError` from an optional proxy dependency in my environment, unrelated to this change. ## Field report Found on a production proxy: two Azure AI OCR deployments on the same account, same document, both HTTP 200 with identical correct text extraction — one billed $0.003/page (in the map), the other $0.00 (not in the map). Nothing in the response distinguishes them, which is what makes this quietly expensive. ## A separate defect noticed while writing the tests Not fixed here, to keep this PR isolated — but worth a look, because it currently breaks OCR tests on this branch: `OCRResponse` (`litellm/llms/base_llm/ocr/transformation.py`) declares a field `object: str = "ocr"` **after** two fields annotated `list[dict[str, object]] | None` (`tables`, `keyValuePairs`). The field named `object` shadows the builtin in the class namespace, so pydantic resolves the annotation to the string `"ocr"` and treats it as a forward-referenced type: ``` pydantic.errors.PydanticUserError: `OCRResponse` is not fully defined; you should define `ocr`, then call `OCRResponse.model_rebuild()`. ``` This reproduces on a clean checkout — `tests/test_litellm/llms/mistral/ocr/test_mistral_ocr_cost.py` currently fails this way (9 failed, 5 passed) with no changes applied. My tests use `model_construct()` to route around it, with a comment saying why. Happy to open a separate issue/PR if useful; annotating those two fields `Any` looks sufficient.

signal.title: fix: map Anthropic API usage-limit errors to RateLimitError (429) not BadRequest (400)
signal.text: ## TLDR **Problem:** Anthropic returns spend/usage-limit exhaustion typed as an `invalid_request_error` (HTTP 400), e.g. *"You have reached your specified API usage limits. You will regain access on … UTC."* LiteLLM faithfully maps that to `BadRequestError` (400), but per the [exception-mapping docs](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/exception_mapping) a usage/rate limit should surface as `RateLimitError` (429). The wrong class breaks callers' retry / fallback handling. **Fix:** Add one phrase branch to the shared `ExceptionCheckers.is_error_str_rate_limit()` helper — the same mechanism already used for Mistral's *"service tier capacity exceeded"* right above it — so an error string containing `"api usage limit"` is detected as a rate limit and mapped to 429. The phrase branches are intentionally ungated by status code, so a limit reported under a 400 is still classified correctly. Fixes #37599 ## Changes - `litellm/litellm_core_utils/exception_mapping_utils.py` - `is_error_str_rate_limit()` now treats Anthropic's `"api usage limit"` phrasing as a rate limit. ## Testing Added `test_anthropic_usage_limit_is_treated_as_rate_limit` in `tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_exception_mapping_utils.py`, using the exact Anthropic payload from the issue and asserting it is detected as a rate limit even under `status_code=400`. ``` tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_exception_mapping_utils.py ... 21 passed ```

signal.title: [Bug]: cache_control blocks silently dropped when routing through SAP AI Core Orchestration (sap/ prefix)
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? When calling ChatLiteLLM with a model on the SAP AI Core Orchestration path (sap/ prefix, e.g. sap/anthropic--claude-4.5-haiku), Anthropic's cache_control parameter is silently stripped before the request reaches Anthropic. No error or warning is raised — the API call succeeds, but cache_read_input_tokens and cache_creation_input_tokens are both 0 on every call regardless of what cache_control markers are set in the messages. Expected: cache_creation_input_tokens > 0 on the first call with a cached prefix, cache_read_input_tokens > 0 on repeat calls with the same prefix. ### User Flow Before a fix: a developer sets cache_control on the system prompt and last message, calls ChatLiteLLM with model="sap/anthropic--claude-4.5-haiku", and expects caching to activate. 1. They construct messages with cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral"} on the system block and last user message 2. They call llm.invoke(messages) via ChatLiteLLM 3. The response metadata shows cache_creation_input_tokens: 0 and cache_read_input_tokens: 0 4. On the second identical call, cache_read_input_tokens is still 0 — caching never activated After a fix: the same call with cache_control set produces cache_creation_input_tokens > 0 on the first call and cache_read_input_tokens > 0 on the second. 1. They construct the same messages with cache_control markers 2. They call llm.invoke(messages) via ChatLiteLLM 3. The response metadata shows cache_creation_input_tokens > 0 4. On the second call with the same prefix, cache_read_input_tokens > 0 ### Proof the bug occurs Config / setup: - litellm==1.83.14, langchain-litellm==0.6.4, Python 3.13 - Provider: SAP AI Core Orchestration (sap/ prefix routing to Anthropic) - Not reproducible with a public LiteLLM proxy — requires SAP AI Core credentials We verified the stripping happens in the LiteLLM/orchestration layer by bypassing it: we wrote a custom BaseChatModel that POSTs the same payload directly to the native Anthropic Messages API via an AI Core foundation-models /invoke deployment. With that path: - cache_control is preserved - cache_creation_input_tokens > 0 on first call - 97.2% cache hit rate and 87% effective input-token cost reduction measured across 169 LLM calls (5-iteration aeval run) The payload we send on the working path (for reference): ``` { "system": [{"type": "text", "text": "...", "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}], "messages": [ ..., {"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "...", "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}]} ] } ``` The same payload routed through ChatLiteLLM (sap/ prefix) results in cache_creation_input_tokens: 0. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? SDK (litellm Python package) ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.83.14 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: fix(responses): stop closing a message item the tool-only stream never opened
signal.text: ## Title fix(responses): stop closing a message item the tool-only stream never opened ## Relevant issues Fixes #37852 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added a testing section to describe the changes below - [x] The unit tests added here fail before the change and pass after it ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `POST /v1/responses` with `stream: true`, against an Anthropic-family model that returns a **tool call with no accompanying text**, emits three events that close a message item that was never opened: ``` response.output_text.done item_id=chatcmpl-<uuid> <-- never had content_part.added response.content_part.done item_id=chatcmpl-<uuid> <-- never had content_part.added response.output_item.done id=chatcmpl-<uuid> <-- never had output_item.added ``` Note the id prefix: `chatcmpl-`, not the `msg_` id used when a message item is opened normally. ### Root cause `_ensure_output_item_for_chunk` has an explicit tool-first branch that opens **no** message item: ```python # Tool-first if hasattr(delta, "tool_calls") and delta.tool_calls: # Tool calls already handled via _queue_tool_call_delta_events # DO NOT create message item return ``` The end of the stream did not mirror that. `return_default_done_events` emitted the message `.done` triple unconditionally, and each `create_*` helper falls back to `self._cached_item_id`, which `_transform_chat_completion_chunk_to_response_api_chunk` had already filled in with the chat completion chunk id. So the ids in the `.done` events are ones no `.added` event ever introduced. Per the Responses API contract every `*.done` must be preceded by its `*.added` for the same `item_id`. Clients that track output items by id reject the stream: the Vercel AI SDK (`ai`, used by CopilotKit and OpenCode) raises `text part <id> not found` and aborts the run **before the tool result is delivered**, so agentic tool-calling loops break on the first tool call. The same request is well formed as soon as the model emits any text alongside the tool call, which is what makes this look intermittent in normal agent use. ### Fix Skip the message `.done` triple when no message item was opened and the turn has no assistant text to report, latching the three sent flags so `is_stream_finished()` still reports done and the stream proceeds to `response.completed`. The guard is deliberately narrow, so the paths that do open a message item are untouched: - `sent_content_part_added_event` is set only where the message item is actually opened, so it is the direct record of "a message item exists". - The `content` / `reasoning_content` check means a turn that has something to report always keeps its `.done` events, including the reasoning-then-tool-call shape where `create_output_content_part_done_event` emits a `reasoning_text` part. - `tool_calls` must be present, so this only applies to the tool-only turn. ## Testing Three tests in `tests/test_litellm/responses/litellm_completion_transformation/test_tool_call_streaming_transformation.py` drive the sync iterator over a whole stream and assert that no `.done` event carries an item id that no `.added` event introduced. ``` # unpatched 1 failed, 8 passed FAILED test_tool_only_turn_does_not_close_a_message_item_it_never_opened # patched 9 passed ``` The other two are controls that pass either way: tool call **with** text, and a plain text-only turn, both of which must keep the full message item lifecycle. Wider control, same tree: ``` python3 -m pytest tests/test_litellm/responses/ -q 469 passed in 59.04s python3 -m pytest tests/test_litellm/test_responses_streaming_container_ownership.py -q 7 passed ``` `ruff check` on both touched files reports exactly the same findings before and after this change (the 12 in `streaming_iterator.py` are pre-existing on the base branch; the test file is clean). **What I did not verify:** I do not have a live proxy with real Anthropic or Bedrock credentials, so this is not confirmed end to end against a real provider. The evidence above is unit-level, driving the real `LiteLLMCompletionStreamingIterator` over a chunk sequence shaped like the one in the issue. Reviewers with proxy access may want to re-run the `curl` from #37852 before merging. ## One thing deliberately left alone `response.completed` also lists an empty message item in `response.output`: ```json {"type": "message", "id": "chatcmpl-...", "status": "completed", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": ""}]} ``` That item is built by `LiteLLMCompletionResponsesConfig.transform_chat_completion_response_to_responses_api_response`, which is shared with the **non-streaming** path. I checked, and a non-streaming `/v1/responses` call for the same tool-only completion returns the identical empty message item, so this is not a streaming bug and removing it would change the response shape for every provider on both paths. It is out of scope here and left for a separate decision. This PR fixes the streaming event pairing, which is what breaks the clients in the report.

signal.title: fix(zai): translate response_format into a forced tool call
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `zai` never forwarded `response_format`, so GLM structured output was impossible - Silent under `drop_params`: proxy returns 200, downstream JSON parsing fails - The existing schema-to-tool-call translation was unreachable from the OpenAI SDK handler How it solves it: - Allowlist `response_format` on `zai` and translate a schema to a forced tool call - Pop the internal `json_mode` flag in the OpenAI SDK handler, as `azure` already does - Unwrap that tool call back into `message.content`, so callers see plain JSON ## User Flow Before: a developer whose app asks a GLM model for JSON against a strict schema gets prose back, and their parser fails on every response 1. They add `model_name: glm-5-turbo` with `litellm_params.model: zai/glm-5-turbo` to the proxy config, with `litellm_settings.drop_params: true` 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"response_format": {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name": "ents", "strict": true, "schema": {...}}}` 3. The response comes back HTTP 200 with `choices[0].message.content` holding prose or a markdown table, not JSON 4. Their app's `json.loads` on that content raises, so every request fails downstream while https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows a clean 200 5. Turning `drop_params` off replaces the silent failure with HTTP 400 `zai does not support parameters: ['response_format']`, so there is no configuration that works After: the same request returns JSON matching the schema they asked for 1. They add the same `glm-5-turbo` deployment to the proxy config, with or without `drop_params` 2. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with the same strict `json_schema` 3. The response comes back HTTP 200 with `choices[0].message.content` holding `{"entities": ["Alice", "service"]}` and `finish_reason: "stop"` 4. Their app's `json.loads` succeeds and the parsed object satisfies the schema ## Relevant issues Fixes #37720 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live calls against the GLM Coding Plan endpoint (`ZAI_API_BASE=https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4`), no mocks. Shared setup for every case below: ```python SCHEMA = {"type": "object", "properties": {"entities": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}}, "required": ["entities"], "additionalProperties": False} RESPONSE_FORMAT = {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name": "ents", "strict": True, "schema": SCHEMA}} PROMPT = 'Extract entities from: "Alice deployed a service."' litellm.completion(model=MODEL, api_base=os.environ["ZAI_API_BASE"], messages=[{"role": "user", "content": PROMPT}], response_format=RESPONSE_FORMAT, max_tokens=3000, drop_params=DROP_PARAMS) ``` ### Before (9432f40145) #### glm-5.3 1. `drop_params=False` -> `litellm.UnsupportedParamsError: zai does not support parameters: ['response_format'], for model=glm-5.3` 2. `drop_params=True` -> HTTP 200, `message.content` is a markdown table: ``` **Entities extracted:** | Entity | Type | |--------|------| | Alice | PERSON | **Notes:** - "Alice" is the only named entity in the sentence (a person's name). - "service" is a generic common noun ... ``` 3. `json.loads` on that content raises `Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)`. SCHEMA-VALID: NO #### glm-5-turbo 1. `drop_params=False` -> `litellm.UnsupportedParamsError: zai does not support parameters: ['response_format'], for model=glm-5-turbo` 2. `drop_params=True` -> HTTP 200, `message.content` is prose: ``` Here are the entities extracted from the sentence: * **Alice** -> Person * **service** -> Software / System / IT Asset *(Note: "deployed" is an action/verb, not an entity)* ``` 3. `json.loads` on that content raises `Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)`. SCHEMA-VALID: NO ### After (95e321cc75) #### glm-5.3 1. `drop_params=False` -> HTTP 200, `message.content` is `{"entities":["Alice", "service"]}` 2. `drop_params=True` -> HTTP 200, `message.content` is `{"entities":["Alice", "deployed", "service"]}` 3. `json.loads` succeeds on both and the object satisfies the schema. SCHEMA-VALID: YES #### glm-5-turbo 1. `drop_params=False` -> HTTP 200, `message.content` is `{"entities":["Alice","service"]}` 2. `drop_params=True` -> HTTP 200, `message.content` is `{"entities":["Alice","service"]}` 3. `json.loads` succeeds on both and the object satisfies the schema. SCHEMA-VALID: YES ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - `glm-4.7` emits no tool call, so it stays unfixed by this - Streaming is deliberately untranslated: a forced tool call cannot be unwrapped mid-stream - `tools` plus `response_format` is untranslated too; nothing could force both - `enforce_validation` still cannot see `response_format` here, unchanged from before - Model metadata (`supports_response_schema`) is still wrong for `zai`; separate PR ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR AI assistance used: Yes Investigation, code, and tests written with Claude Code.

signal.title: [Feature]: support model discovery with custom provider
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### The Feature Here is an example of how the desired config.yaml could look: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: my-custom-service/* # Use a wildcard for the custom provider group litellm_params: model: custom_openai/* # The litellm provider identifier api_key: os.environ/MY_CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY api_base: "http://my-custom-provider-url.com/v1" # The endpoint for the custom provider litellm_settings: check_provider_endpoint: true # Enable model discovery ``` With this configuration, a call to the LiteLLM proxy's /v1/models endpoint should trigger a discovery call to http://my-custom-provider-url.com/v1/models and return the result in the expected format. This enhancement would significantly improve the integration of LiteLLM with the rapidly growing ecosystem of self-hosted and third-party OpenAI-compatible APIs. Thank you for considering this feature request ### Motivation, pitch The new Model Discovery feature is an excellent addition for dynamically fetching a list of available models from a provider when using a wildcard in the configuration (e.g., xai/*, openai/*). This works well for the list of officially supported providers. However, this functionality does not seem to extend to custom providers, specifically those that are OpenAI-compatible and configured using the custom_openai provider type. When using a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint (like a private VLLM server, another LLM proxy, or a niche provider), we are still required to manually list every single model ID in the config.yaml. This is not scalable and requires manual configuration updates whenever the upstream provider adds or removes a model. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? signal.title: fix: omit thinking.type=disabled for always-on thinking Claude models
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` forwarded verbatim to Fable/Mythos models - those models 400: "thinking.type.disabled is not supported for this model" - routers retargeting requests across model generations hit this constantly How it solves it: - new cost map flag `thinking_always_on` on Fable/Mythos entries - Anthropic, /v1/messages, and Bedrock Converse transforms omit the param when flagged - omission is the API documented remedy; model thinks adaptively by default ## User Flow Before: a caller whose request was valid on Claude Sonnet 4.5 gets a 400 when a router sends the same request to Claude Fable 5 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"model": "claude-fable-5"`, `"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}` 2. The response is a 400 with `"thinking.type.disabled" is not supported for this model. Thinking defaults to adaptive mode when not specified` 3. The same body against a router model group fails the whole request whenever the router picks a Fable 5 deployment, even though the request was valid on the model the caller originally targeted After: the same request succeeds; the model thinks adaptively as the API prescribes 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"model": "claude-fable-5"`, `"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}` 2. The response is a 200 with the model's normal content; the gateway omitted the unsupported param and logged a warning 3. Requests carrying `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` to models that accept it (Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.8, Opus 5, Sonnet 5) are forwarded byte for byte, unchanged ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Setup: local proxy on :4620 from this branch, `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`, real Postgres, models `claude-fable-5` and `claude-sonnet-4-5` served through a live Anthropic-compatible upstream (real provider account for this repo is out of credit; the upstream is the team's live gateway hitting the real Anthropic API, so requests, money, and the 400 are real). Config: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: claude-fable-5 litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-fable-5 api_base: https://<gateway-host> api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN - model_name: claude-sonnet-4-5 litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 api_base: https://<gateway-host> api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` ### Before (4bb3152cc5) #### /v1/messages, claude-fable-5, thinking disabled 1. `curl -s -w "HTTP %{http_code}" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4620/v1/messages -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"claude-fable-5","max_tokens":64,"thinking":{"type":"disabled"},"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi repro leg 1"}]}'` 2. `HTTP 400` with `"\"thinking.type.disabled\" is not supported for this model. Thinking defaults to adaptive mode when not specified; use \"thinking.type.enabled\" with \"budget_tokens\" for extended thinking"` #### /v1/chat/completions, claude-fable-5, thinking disabled 1. Same body against http://127.0.0.1:4620/v1/chat/completions 2. `HTTP 400`, `litellm.BadRequestError: AnthropicException` wrapping the same provider error #### /v1/messages, claude-sonnet-4-5, thinking disabled (negative control) 1. Same body with `"model": "claude-sonnet-4-5"` 2. `HTTP 200`, normal text content (this model accepts disabled) ### After (b95d3cef31) #### /v1/messages, claude-fable-5, thinking disabled 1. Same curl as Before 2. `HTTP 200`, content starts with an adaptive thinking block then text; proxy log shows `Dropping thinking={'type': 'disabled'} for model=claude-fable-5: thinking is always on for this model and cannot be disabled (the alternative is a provider 400). The model will still think adaptively, its response can contain thinking blocks, and those thinking tokens are billed as output tokens.` #### /v1/chat/completions, claude-fable-5, thinking disabled 1. Same curl as Before (max_tokens 2048 so text survives the thinking budget) 2. `HTTP 200`, `content: "Hi! ..."`, `model: claude-fable-5` #### /v1/messages, claude-sonnet-4-5, thinking disabled (negative control) 1. Same curl as Before 2. `HTTP 200`, normal text content, request body forwarded unchanged (no warning logged) ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Bedrock Converse arm covered by unit tests only; no AWS credentials in this rig - /v1/responses already converts `thinking` to `reasoning`, never forwards disabled - Opus 5 `disabled` plus `output_config.effort xhigh/max` is a caller contradiction, untouched - unmapped future Fable/Mythos ids covered by a `fallback_generalizations` rule ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Changes request transformation for Anthropic thinking params across chat, messages, and Bedrock Converse. Scope is narrow (only drop `type=disabled` when flagged), but a wrong flag would silently enable thinking and bill thinking tokens. > > **Overview** > Stops Fable/Mythos (and similar always-on-thinking Claude families) from 400ing when a caller or router forwards `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}`. Those models reject disable; omitting the param is the documented fallback to adaptive thinking. > > Adds a cost-map flag `thinking_always_on` on Fable/Mythos entries plus a `claude-(fable|mythos)-` fallback rule for unmapped ids. `AnthropicModelInfo.maybe_drop_disabled_thinking` strips only that exact shape (with a warning) on Anthropic chat, `/v1/messages`, and Bedrock Converse. Models that accept `disabled` (Opus/Sonnet 5, Opus 4.8, legacy) still get it unchanged. > > Also hoists the duplicated `local_model_cost_map` pytest fixture into shared conftest so capability tests hit the in-repo map. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit b95d3cef31d3c5a2fb4abedfe395ec224401bad9. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: fix(ollama): fix streaming tool call finish_reason, arguments format, and parallel index
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Streamed tool calls through `ollama_chat` ended with `finish_reason: "stop"` instead of `"tool_calls"` - `function.arguments` arrived as a dict instead of a JSON string in streaming - Parallel tool calls all got `index: 0`, merging them into one malformed call - Each streaming chunk got a different response `id` and tool call ids lacked the `call_` prefix How it solves it: - Track `saw_tool_calls` across chunks and upgrade `finish_reason` on the done chunk, gated on `"stop"` so `"length"` passes through - Serialize dict arguments to JSON strings in the streaming chunk parser - Track a persistent `_tool_call_index` counter so each tool call gets a sequential index - Generate a stable `response_id` once per stream and prefix tool call ids with `call_` ## User Flow Before: a developer using an OpenAI-compatible client through a LiteLLM proxy to an Ollama backend sends a request that triggers two parallel tool calls, but only the first call survives and its arguments are corrupted 1. They send `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `"stream": true`, two tools, and a message asking for both 2. The SSE stream delivers two `delta.tool_calls` chunks, both with `"index": 0` 3. Their client accumulates both calls into the same slot, concatenating arguments into `{"city": "Tokyo"}{"timezone": "America/New_York"}` 4. The final chunk arrives with `"finish_reason": "stop"`, so the client treats the turn as ordinary text and never dispatches the tools After: the same request delivers each tool call with a unique index and the correct finish reason, so the client dispatches both 1. They send the same `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `"stream": true`, two tools, and the same message 2. The SSE stream delivers two `delta.tool_calls` chunks, the first with `"index": 0` and the second with `"index": 1` 3. Their client accumulates each call into its own slot, preserving both argument objects 4. The final chunk arrives with `"finish_reason": "tool_calls"`, so the client dispatches both tools ## Relevant issues Fixes #33678 Fixes #35663 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Proxy config: `ollama_chat` route to a remote Ollama instance. Real streaming LLM calls, no mocks. Anonymized endpoint and key. Request payload used for all cases: ```json {"model": "ollama_chat/<model>", "stream": true, "tools": [ {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_weather", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["city"]}}}, {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_time", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"timezone": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["timezone"]}}} ], "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the weather in Tokyo and the time in New York? Call both tools."}]} ``` ### Before (ff02d5cfc0) #### Parallel tool calls (separate chunks) 1. `curl -sN http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '<payload above with model ollama_chat/glm-5.1>'` 2. Tool call chunks arrive with both indices set to 0: ``` data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"tool_calls":[{"id":"call_...","function":{"arguments":"{\"city\": \"Tokyo\"}","name":"get_weather"},"type":"function","index":0}]}}]} data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"tool_calls":[{"id":"call_...","function":{"arguments":"{\"timezone\": \"America/New_York\"}","name":"get_time"},"type":"function","index":0}]}}]} data: {"choices":[{"delta":{},"finish_reason":"stop"}]} ``` 3. The final chunk reports `"finish_reason": "stop"` instead of `"tool_calls"`, and both tool calls share `"index": 0` #### Single tool call 1. Same request with one tool and a single-call prompt 2. Tool call chunk arrives with `"finish_reason": "stop"` on the done chunk, tool call id without `call_` prefix #### Plain text (no tools) 1. Same request without `tools` array 2. Final chunk reports `"finish_reason": "stop"` (correct, unaffected) ### After (04694c13a6) #### Parallel tool calls (separate chunks) 1. `curl -sN http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '<payload above with model ollama_chat/glm-5.1>'` 2. Tool call chunks arrive with sequential indices: ``` data: {"id":"eed04fdd-...","choices":[{"delta":{"tool_calls":[{"id":"call_7bc17b2c-...","function":{"arguments":"{\"city\": \"Tokyo\"}","name":"get_weather"},"type":"function","index":0}]}}]} data: {"id":"eed04fdd-...","choices":[{"delta":{"tool_calls":[{"id":"call_30ea4e4a-...","function":{"arguments":"{\"timezone\": \"America/New_York\"}","name":"get_time"},"type":"function","index":1}]}}]} data: {"id":"eed04fdd-...","choices":[{"delta":{},"finish_reason":"tool_calls"}]} ``` 3. Both tool calls have unique indices (`0` and `1`), unique `call_`-prefixed ids, arguments are JSON strings, and the final chunk reports `"finish_reason": "tool_calls"` #### Parallel tool calls (same chunk) 1. Same payload with model `ollama_chat/qwen3.5:397b` 2. Both tool calls arrive in a single delta with correct indices: ``` data: {"id":"69e2eead-...","choices":[{"delta":{"tool_calls":[ {"id":"call_cef017c0-...","function":{"arguments":"{\"city\": \"Tokyo\"}","name":"get_weather"},"type":"function","index":0}, {"id":"call_dc041897-...","function":{"arguments":"{\"timezone\": \"New York\"}","name":"get_time"},"type":"function","index":1} ]}}]} data: {"id":"69e2eead-...","choices":[{"delta":{},"finish_reason":"tool_calls"}]} ``` #### Single tool call 1. Same request with one tool and a single-call prompt 2. Tool call chunk has `call_`-prefixed id, JSON string arguments, and done chunk reports `"finish_reason": "tool_calls"` #### Plain text (no tools) 1. Same request without `tools` array 2. Final chunk reports `"finish_reason": "stop"` (correct, unaffected) #### Length truncation with tool calls 1. Same request with `"max_tokens": 1` and a tool-warranted prompt 2. Final chunk reports `"finish_reason": "length"` (not overridden to `"tool_calls"`, preserving the truncation signal) ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Only `ollama_chat/` streaming is fixed; `ollama/` (generate endpoint) streaming tool calls are a separate problem tracked in #35711 - The `finish_reason` override is gated on `"stop"` to preserve `"length"` and other non-stop reasons, matching the existing `streaming_handler.py` finalizer ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: feat(ui): add and delete auto-router tiers with classifier definitions
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The tier list in the auto-router forms is fixed at four - The backend's tier_definitions (stacked PR below) has no UI - Custom tiers need a definition the classifier can use How it solves it: - An Edit tiers button after the Reasoning tier - Remove any built-in tier, restore it, or add custom tiers - Every new tier requires a name, a definition, and models - The definition becomes that tier's bullet in the classifier rubric - Going custom forces the LLM classifier and shows a Fallback Tier select - Escalation, adaptive, session pinning, and display names disable with a hint - An untouched tier set submits a payload identical to today's ## User Flow Before: an operator wants a SECURITY_REVIEW tier and the form cannot express it 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=models-and-endpoints, Add Model, Auto Router tab, and expand Detailed Configuration 2. The Complexity Tier Configuration section shows exactly four tiers with no way to add or remove one 3. Their only options are renaming a tier or hand-writing tier_definitions in raw config and restarting the proxy After: the same form edits the tier set directly 1. signal.title: fix(responses): preserve Bedrock Mantle validation errors
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Bedrock Mantle validation failures reach callers as status 500 - The upstream 400 response is treated like a connection failure How it solves it: - Routes Bedrock Mantle through the existing Bedrock status mapping - Preserves `BadRequestError`, status 400, and the upstream message ## User Flow Before: a Responses API caller receives the wrong error class for an invalid request 1. They send `POST https://bedrock-mantle.us-east-1.api.aws/openai/v1/responses` with a Responses request 2. Mantle rejects the request with HTTP 400 and an `invalid_request_error` body 3. The caller receives `APIConnectionError` with status 500 and cannot distinguish validation from connectivity After: the same invalid request is reported as a client error 1. They send `POST https://bedrock-mantle.us-east-1.api.aws/openai/v1/responses` with the same Responses request 2. Mantle rejects the request with HTTP 400 and an `invalid_request_error` body 3. The caller receives `BadRequestError` with status 400 and the upstream validation message ## Relevant issues Addresses the error-classification portion of #36546 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile Confidence Score of at least 4/5 before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The before run was captured against commit `bea31871fc` with a mocked HTTP 400 response. Both sync and async `litellm.responses()` paths raised `APIConnectionError` with status 500 The after run was captured against commit `f6f6044e09` with the same mocked HTTP 400 response. signal.title: litellm-ai-gateway panics on first outbound TLS connection — "no process-level CryptoProvider available" (rustls 0.23)
signal.text: ### Summary The standalone Rust gateway server (`litellm-ai-gateway`, `server` feature) panics on the first outbound TLS connection to a provider (e.g. `api.anthropic.com`). The panic is caught by the tokio runtime so the process stays alive, but the request that triggered it fails with a generic 502. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Build `litellm-ai-gateway` from `litellm-rust/` with the `server` feature enabled 2. Run it standalone (Mode 2, not embedded in the Python proxy) with any provider key configured 3. Send a request that requires an outbound HTTPS call (e.g. `POST /v1/messages` with an Anthropic key) ### Actual Behavior ``` thread 'tokio-rt-worker' (7) panicked at rustls-0.23.42/src/crypto/mod.rs:249:14: Could not automatically determine the process-level CryptoProvider from Rustls crate features. Call CryptoProvider::install_default() before this point to select a provider manually, or make sure exactly one of the 'aws-lc-rs' and 'ring' features is enabled. ``` The pod/process doesn't crash (panic is caught per-task), but the request fails — client sees `502 {"error":{"message":"messages provider request failed"}}` instead of a real response (or a real auth error, if the key is invalid). ### Root Cause `litellm-rust/Cargo.lock` currently resolves **two rustls versions** (0.21.12 and 0.23.42), and both the `ring` and `aws-lc-rs` crypto backend crates are present in the dependency tree (pulled in transitively by different dependencies). Nothing in the workspace calls `rustls::crypto::CryptoProvider::install_default()`, so rustls has no way to pick a process-wide default crypto provider — the first TLS handshake panics. This is a well-known rustls 0.23+ footgun when a dependency tree ends up with multiple crypto backends (see e.g. lightningdevkit/ldk-node#991, alloy-rs/alloy#874, openobserve/openobserve#7200 for the same failure mode in other projects). ### Suggested Fix Call `CryptoProvider::install_default()` once at process startup (before any TLS connection is attempted), e.g.: ```rust rustls::crypto::ring::default_provider() .install_default() .expect("failed to install rustls crypto provider"); ``` or align the dependency tree so only one of `ring`/`aws-lc-rs` is enabled. ### Environment - Built from source at the workspace's current `master` as of 2026-08-21 (includes #37241, routing `/chat/completions` through the Rust core) - Deployed standalone (Mode 2) on GKE, tested with a placeholder Anthropic key

signal.title: feat(newrelic): per-team cost and usage metrics via team callbacks
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Teams need their LLM spend visible in their own New Relic account - New Relic's AI monitoring has token counts but no cost anywhere - No per-team metrics path existed, only traces How it solves it: - The same `newrelic` team callback now also emits Metric API data - Batched counts for requests, cost, tokens plus a latency summary - Each team's metrics post with that team's own ingest key ## User Flow Before: a team lead cannot chart their LiteLLM spend in their New Relic account 1. Admin configures POST https://litellm-domain/team/{team_id}/callback with `newrelic_api_key` and `newrelic_region` (traces PR) 2. The team's traces arrive, but `FROM Metric SELECT * WHERE metricName LIKE 'litellm%'` in their account returns nothing 3. The team has no way to alert on spend or request volume in New Relic After: the same configuration also delivers per-team metrics 1. Admin configures the same team callback, nothing new to set up 2. Developers on the team send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions requests as usual 3. Within a minute `FROM Metric SELECT sum(litellm.cost.usd), sum(litellm.requests), sum(litellm.tokens.total) FACET team_alias, model, status` shows the team's traffic with real dollar cost 4. Another team's requests in the same window add nothing to this account ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5095 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Stacked on the traces PR (#37603); base for the run below is that branch. Shared setup: proxy with one Gemini model, `LITELLM_OTEL_V2=true`, team tenant-a carrying the `newrelic` callback with a real ingest key for account 8412808, team tenant-b with no New Relic callback. Real Gemini calls. ### Before (d77f6b6b6a, traces PR head) 1. Three tenant-a completions through the proxy return 200 2. `FROM Metric SELECT * WHERE metricName LIKE 'litellm%' SINCE 10 minutes ago` against account 8412808 returns no rows (only Span data exists) ### After (eae95f6443) 1. `for i in 1 2 3; do curl http://127.0.0.1:14196/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_A" -d '{"model": "gemini-flash", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say: m'$i'"}]}'; done` -> three 200s 2. One tenant-b completion in the same window -> 200 3. NRQL a minute later: `FROM Metric SELECT sum(litellm.cost.usd), sum(litellm.requests), sum(litellm.tokens.total) FACET team_alias, model, status SINCE 10 minutes ago` returns exactly one facet row: `tenant-a / gemini/gemini-3.7-flash / success` with `sum.litellm.cost.usd: 0.00069375`, `sum.litellm.requests: 3`, `sum.litellm.tokens.total: 197` 4. The same window's `FROM Span SELECT count(*)` still shows the 3 traces, so both signals flow side by side ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Stacked on #37603; merge that first, then retarget this to staging - Cost emits `response_cost` as-is, guardrail component included - 4xx batches drop with a logged warning; 5xx re-queue capped at 10k records - One team callback yields two logger instances (metrics plus traces); identity dedup prevents double dispatch - Metric API endpoint rides the same fixed us/eu table as traces ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR --- --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches team ingest-key routing and logger cache eviction, so credential isolation and flush/retry behavior need careful review, but it is additive observability rather than a change to auth or request handling. > > **Overview** > The existing team `newrelic` callback now ships **cost and usage metrics** into that team's New Relic account (Metric API), alongside traces. Requests, USD cost, prompt/completion/total tokens, and a duration summary are batched by team, model, provider, and status. > > Credentials are **injected only** from proxy-stamped team callback vars (`newrelic_api_key` / `newrelic_region`). There is no env-key fallback, so a team's metrics never use the operator license key. Request-body params cannot redirect the team's key to another region. > > Per-team loggers are cached and flushed on a timer. 4xx (including 403) drops the batch; 5xx/network requeues with a cap. Cache eviction calls `stop()` and drains remaining records so flush tasks do not leak and queued metrics are not silently discarded. With team creds, the callback name still also dispatches the global trace logger. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 5222c9575e957675938a3f9ffee00beb90e8fda0. signal.title: feat(proxy): add router_model_name to auto-routed response bodies
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Auto-routed model is only in `x-litellm-model-id`, a header - SDKs that hide response headers cannot read the routed model - Streaming makes it worse: no body surface at all How it solves it: - Adds `router_model_name` to the response body - Present on both non-streaming bodies and every SSE chunk - Emitted only when an auto-routing strategy actually picked the model ## User Flow Before: a developer whose app streams chat completions through an auto-router cannot tell which model answered, so their UI cannot label the response 1. They configure a `smart-route` model group backed by a complexity router with `fast-model`, `standard-model`, and `deep-model` tiers 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "smart-route"` and `"stream": true` 3. Each SSE frame comes back with `"model": "smart-route"`, the alias they sent, and nothing naming the tier that actually ran 4. The routed model is in the `x-litellm-model-id` response header, which their SDK does not expose to application code 5. Their UI renders every answer unlabeled, whether a cheap tier or an expensive one served it 6. Sending the same request without `"stream": true` gives the same result: the body names only the alias After: the same developer reads the routed model straight off the body, streaming included 1. They configure a `smart-route` model group backed by a complexity router with `fast-model`, `standard-model`, and `deep-model` tiers 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "smart-route"` and `"stream": true` 3. Each SSE frame comes back with `"model": "smart-route"` and `"router_model_name": "deep-model"`, naming the tier that actually ran 4. They read the routed model from the frame their SDK already hands them, with no access to response headers needed 5. Their UI labels each answer with the tier that served it 6. Sending the same request without `"stream": true` puts the same `"router_model_name"` on the response body A request that names a model group directly, with no auto-routing involved, has no `router_model_name` key at all, so nothing changes for callers who do not use an auto-router ## Relevant issues - The response body `model` field is deliberately restamped back to the client-requested alias on both the streaming and non-streaming paths, which is correct OpenAI semantics, so this adds a separate namespaced key rather than redefining `model` - `router_model_name` carries the model group the router selected, not the raw upstream provider string, so it matches the names an operator wrote in their config - Router fallbacks resolve on the first `__anext__`, after the streaming wrapper is handed back, so each chunk reads the selected group live instead of a snapshot taken before the router had decided. A fallback onto a plain group drops the key, and one onto another auto-routed group reports the new tier - langchain-openai builds `response_metadata` from a fixed key list, so LangChain users read this off the raw chunk rather than off `response_metadata` - Removes a redundant function-local import in the streaming generator that shadowed the module-level one and made the whole name function-local ## Documentation Docs PR: [BerriAI/litellm-docs#982](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm-docs/pull/982). Adds a `Reading the picked model from the response` section to the auto routing page covering the field shape on streaming and non-streaming responses, what value it carries, the two cases it is absent in, and the langchain-openai workaround; cross-linked from the response headers page. ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy on a complexity router with three tiers, hitting real Bedrock and Anthropic models through a gateway. Same five commands both runs Config used: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: fast-model litellm_params: {model: openai/bedrock/global.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0, api_base: os.environ/GW_BASE, api_key: os.environ/GW_KEY} - model_name: standard-model litellm_params: {model: openai/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, api_base: os.environ/GW_BASE, api_key: os.environ/GW_KEY} - model_name: deep-model litellm_params: {model: openai/bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0, api_base: os.environ/GW_BASE, api_key: os.environ/GW_KEY} - model_name: smart-route litellm_params: model: auto_router/complexity_router complexity_router_default_model: standard-model complexity_router_config: classifier_type: llm classifier_llm_config: {model: fast-model, timeout_ms: 15000} tier_definitions: - {name: CASUAL, description: greetings, chitchat, and quick factual questions with short known answers} - {name: CODING, description: any programming task, code review, debugging, or software design work} - {name: RESEARCH, description: multi-step analysis, proofs, tradeoff studies, or open-ended research-grade reasoning} fallback_tier: CODING tiers: {CASUAL: fast-model, CODING: standard-model, RESEARCH: deep-model} ``` Commands: ```bash P=4405; K=sk-mib-master ask () { printf '{"model":"smart-route",%s"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"%s"}]}' "$2" "$1"; } echo "### 1. non-streaming, auto-routed" curl -s http://localhost:$P/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $K" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d "$(ask 'Derive the time complexity of binary search and prove the bound' '')" \ | jq '{model, router_model_name}' echo "### 2. streaming, auto-routed, first SSE frame" curl -sN http://localhost:$P/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $K" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d "$(ask 'Derive the time complexity of binary search and prove the bound' '"stream":true,')" \ | grep -m1 '^data: {' echo "### 3. streaming, a different tier wins, first SSE frame" curl -sN http://localhost:$P/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $K" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d "$(ask 'hey there' '"stream":true,')" | grep -m1 '^data: {' echo "### 4. streaming, review a function so the coding tier wins, first SSE frame" curl -sN http://localhost:$P/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $K" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d "$(ask 'Review this Python function for bugs: def add(a, b): return a - b' '"stream":true,')" \ | grep -m1 '^data: {' echo "### 5. negative control: direct model group, no auto-routing, key must be absent" curl -s http://localhost:$P/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $K" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"standard-model","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hey there"}]}' \ | jq '{model, has_router_model_name: has("router_model_name")}' ``` Before, at merge base `e07a7129c5`: ``` ### 1. non-streaming, auto-routed { "model": "smart-route", "router_model_name": null } ### 2. streaming, auto-routed, first SSE frame data: {"id":"chatcmpl-cca8a3f7-5661-436e-8d71-35261d4db817","object":"chat.completion.chunk","created":1787262634,"model":"smart-route","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"role":"assistant","content":"# "}}]} ### 3. streaming, a different tier wins, first SSE frame data: {"id":"chatcmpl-68c41926-3e06-4a86-9290-b01f1a4c891f","created":1787262637,"model":"smart-route","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"Hey","role":"assistant"}}],"provider_specific_fields":{}} ### 4. streaming, review a function so the coding tier wins, first SSE frame data: {"id":"chatcmpl-e866c795-9173-467f-96a4-72861824102f","object":"chat.completion.chunk","created":1787262640,"model":"smart-route","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"role":"assistant","content":"#"}}]} ### 5. negative control: direct model group, no auto-routing, key must be absent { "model": "standard-model", "has_router_model_name": false } ``` `null` in section 1 is jq rendering a key that is not there, matching the `has(...)` check in section 5 After, at PR tip: ``` ### 1. non-streaming, auto-routed { "model": "smart-route", "router_model_name": "deep-model" } ### 2. streaming, auto-routed, first SSE frame data: {"id":"chatcmpl-c27b92d7-c374-49ea-8473-828acec9cd50","created":1787263277,"model":"smart-route","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"#","role":"assistant"}}],"provider_specific_fields":{},"router_model_name":"deep-model"} ### 3. streaming, a different tier wins, first SSE frame data: {"id":"chatcmpl-f1344858-017f-43ca-81fc-e97175bbac45","created":1787263280,"model":"smart-route","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"Hey! How's","role":"assistant"}}],"provider_specific_fields":{},"router_model_name":"fast-model"} ### 4. streaming, review a function so the coding tier wins, first SSE frame data: {"id":"chatcmpl-f5be4eb0-975d-4a2d-ac0a-8b6e0122df81","object":"chat.completion.chunk","created":1787263282,"model":"smart-route","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"role":"assistant","content":"#"}}],"router_model_name":"standard-model"} ### 5. negative control: direct model group, no auto-routing, key must be absent { "model": "standard-model", "has_router_model_name": false } ``` Three different prompts route to three different tiers, each one named in the body, and the direct-group control stays clean ### Mid-stream fallback Review raised that a fallback taken during iteration could keep naming the tier that already failed. Reproduced against a `smart-route-fb` group whose RESEARCH tier points at an upstream that completes the HTTP handshake and then resets the socket, which is what makes the router resolve its fallback lazily on the first `__anext__` rather than before the wrapper is handed back. `router_settings.fallbacks` sends `smart-route-fb` to the plain `standard-model` group. Extra config for this run: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: dead-model litellm_params: {model: openai/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, api_base: http://127.0.0.1:18477/v1, api_key: sk-dead} - model_name: smart-route-fb litellm_params: model: auto_router/complexity_router complexity_router_default_model: standard-model complexity_router_config: classifier_type: llm classifier_llm_config: {model: fast-model, timeout_ms: 15000} tier_definitions: - {name: CASUAL, description: greetings, chitchat, and quick factual questions with short known answers} - {name: RESEARCH, description: multi-step analysis, proofs, tradeoff studies, or open-ended research-grade reasoning} fallback_tier: RESEARCH tiers: {CASUAL: fast-model, RESEARCH: dead-model} router_settings: fallbacks: [{"smart-route-fb": ["standard-model"]}] num_retries: 0 ``` Port 18477 is a raw socket server that answers with `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`, `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, then resets the connection with `SO_LINGER`. A refused connection is not enough here: it makes `acompletion` raise before returning the wrapper, so the fallback resolves eagerly and the snapshot is already correct Commands: ```bash P=4405; K=sk-mib-master frames () { grep '^data: {' | head -3 | jq -Rc 'ltrimstr("data: ")|fromjson|{model, router_model_name:(.router_model_name // "<ABSENT>")}'; } echo "### streaming, the auto-routed tier dies after the handshake, router falls back to a plain group" curl -sN http://localhost:$P/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $K" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"smart-route-fb","stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Derive the time complexity of binary search and prove the bound"}]}' | frames echo "### regression, no fallback, the tier is still named on every frame" curl -sN http://localhost:$P/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $K" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"smart-route","stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Derive the time complexity of binary search and prove the bound"}]}' | frames ``` Before, at the reviewed sha `92b057c641`, which snapshotted the selected group once before iteration: ``` ### streaming, the auto-routed tier dies after the handshake, router falls back to a plain group {"model":"standard-model","router_model_name":"dead-model"} {"model":"standard-model","router_model_name":"dead-model"} {"model":"standard-model","router_model_name":"dead-model"} ### regression, no fallback, the tier is still named on every frame {"model":"smart-route","router_model_name":"deep-model"} {"model":"smart-route","router_model_name":"deep-model"} {"model":"smart-route","router_model_name":"deep-model"} ``` Every frame credits `dead-model`, the tier that served none of the content After, at PR tip, reading the selected group per chunk instead: ``` ### streaming, the auto-routed tier dies after the handshake, router falls back to a plain group {"model":"standard-model","router_model_name":"<ABSENT>"} {"model":"standard-model","router_model_name":"<ABSENT>"} {"model":"standard-model","router_model_name":"<ABSENT>"} ### regression, no fallback, the tier is still named on every frame {"model":"smart-route","router_model_name":"deep-model"} {"model":"smart-route","router_model_name":"deep-model"} {"model":"smart-route","router_model_name":"deep-model"} ``` The fallback lands outside any auto-routed group, so the key drops rather than naming a tier that did not run, and the happy path is unchanged. A fallback onto a second auto-routed group reports that group's tier instead, covered by unit tests <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches proxy response shaping and router metadata on the hot completion/streaming path. Additive and gated to auto-routed requests, but a stamp/clear bug could mislabel the serving model or leak the field onto ordinary group traffic. > > **Overview** > Adds a body-level `router_model_name` so clients can see which auto-router tier actually served a request. The existing `model` field stays the client alias; the new field is emitted only when an auto-routing strategy actually picked the group. > > The router stamps `_auto_routed_request` on a successful pre-routing hook and clears it on plain-group re-entry (fallbacks reuse the same kwargs). The proxy copies `deployment_model_name` onto dict and object responses, including the fast SSE serializer. Streaming reads the selected group per chunk so a mid-stream fallback drops the key or reports the new tier instead of a stale snapshot. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit b31cd8e7bfb76f46fd41d42f16a9b51b43f1c27d. signal.title: fix(spend): bound each spend-log write statement by row count as well as bytes
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Spend-log writes are bounded by bytes, not rows - Small rows never reach the byte budget, so nothing binds - Every write statement stays at 1000 rows forever - The query engine keeps ~110 MB per worker that nothing frees How it solves it: - Adds a row budget beside the existing byte budget - Whichever budget binds first splits the statement - Default 100 rows, measured 6x less resident engine memory ## User Flow Before: an operator whose proxy does not store prompts sees pod memory sit far above what traffic explains, and the knob documented for exactly this does nothing 1. They deploy the proxy with `store_prompts_in_spend_logs` left off and serve normal traffic through `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` 2. They exec into a pod and run `ps -eo pid,rss,cmd --sort=-rss`, and the Prisma query engine line shows roughly 110 MB more resident than it did at startup 3. They stop sending traffic and wait, then run the same `ps`, and the number has not moved 4. Their autoscaler, configured on memory, holds the replica count at whatever the peak set 5. They read the docs, lower `SPEND_LOG_WRITE_BATCH_MAX_BYTES` to 200000, restart the pod, repeat the traffic, and the engine's resident memory is unchanged, because their rows never came near even the old budget After: the same deployment holds a fraction of that, and there is a budget that actually responds 1. They deploy the proxy with `store_prompts_in_spend_logs` left off and serve normal traffic through `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` 2. They exec into a pod and run `ps -eo pid,rss,cmd --sort=-rss`, and the Prisma query engine line shows roughly 18 MB more resident than at startup 3. They stop sending traffic and wait, and as before the number does not move, but it is six times lower 4. Their autoscaler tracks something much closer to real load 5. If they want it lower still they set `SPEND_LOG_WRITE_BATCH_MAX_ROWS` to 50, restart, and the number drops again ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5926 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile Confidence Score of at least 4/5 before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, identical for both sides. Postgres 16 in a container, and the proxy image `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-latest` with the tree under test mounted at `/src` and `PYTHONPATH=/src`, so the two sides differ only by source. That image carries Prisma query engine 5.4.2. Every leg prints which tree it loaded and whether the new budget is present, so a leg can never be mistaken for its sibling. ``` docker run -d --name lit4765-pg -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=... -e POSTGRES_USER=litellm -e POSTGRES_DB=litellm -p 5476:5432 postgres:16 ``` Engine resident memory is read from `/proc/<engine pid>/status`, sampled 30s after the flush returns so it is what the pod keeps, not a transient peak. `probe_flush.py` drives the real `ProxyUpdateSpend.update_spend_logs`, so the whole shipped path runs. The two arms are interleaved (staging, fix, staging, fix, ...) so table growth and machine drift hit both equally. ### Before (35416c702d) #### Case 1: real traffic through a live proxy 1. Boot the proxy on the staging tree and send 5 real OpenAI chat completions: ``` $ /app/.venv/bin/python -c 'import litellm.proxy.utils as u; print("MARKER_SPEND_LOG_WRITE_BATCH_MAX_ROWS:", getattr(u, "SPEND_LOG_WRITE_BATCH_MAX_ROWS", "ABSENT"))' MARKER_SPEND_LOG_WRITE_BATCH_MAX_ROWS: ABSENT $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." \ -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly the word: ok"}],"max_tokens":12}' call 1 -> HTTP 200 id=chatcmpl-EF947qTpmRQFlUgWiQlm1xYZnIPB1 content='ok' call 2 -> HTTP 200 id=chatcmpl-EF947GXunHa2sBHqwDszkIkYBQXwN content='ok' call 3 -> HTTP 200 id=chatcmpl-EF949FhdRQJt02YNLBRobyHZbR9kp content='ok' call 4 -> HTTP 200 id=chatcmpl-EF94AlD4Ab8HSOgs0fkqSatbFGSFj content='ok' call 5 -> HTTP 200 id=chatcmpl-EF94C9oZ8oHewJa8y3wN17hngFiOC content='ok' ``` 2. Wait for the flush and read back what those calls wrote: ``` spend log rows found for those 5 call ids: 5 request_id=chatcmpl-EF947GXunHa2sBHqwDszkIkYBQXwN model=openai/gpt-4o-mini spend=0.00000270 total_tokens=15 status=success request_id=chatcmpl-EF947qTpmRQFlUgWiQlm1xYZnIPB1 model=openai/gpt-4o-mini spend=0.00000270 total_tokens=15 status=success request_id=chatcmpl-EF949FhdRQJt02YNLBRobyHZbR9kp model=openai/gpt-4o-mini spend=0.00000270 total_tokens=15 status=success request_id=chatcmpl-EF94AlD4Ab8HSOgs0fkqSatbFGSFj model=openai/gpt-4o-mini spend=0.00000270 total_tokens=15 status=success request_id=chatcmpl-EF94C9oZ8oHewJa8y3wN17hngFiOC model=openai/gpt-4o-mini spend=0.00000270 total_tokens=15 status=success total real spend for this run: $0.00001350 ``` #### Case 2: the flush at production scale 1. Drive the real flush with 50,000 rows shaped like a `store_prompts_in_spend_logs=false` deployment, three times, interleaved with the After arm: ``` STAGING max_rows=None retained=113.0 MB flush=6.16s all_rows_persisted=True (50000) STAGING max_rows=None retained=121.0 MB flush=6.00s all_rows_persisted=True (50000) STAGING max_rows=None retained=107.0 MB flush=6.55s all_rows_persisted=True (50000) ``` 2. Confirm the byte budget is not what is missing. Sweep the statement size directly against the same database, 200,000 rows each, with the 2 MB byte budget in force throughout: ``` 1000 rows/stmt -> 179.0 MB retained 500 rows/stmt -> 91.0 MB retained 250 rows/stmt -> 41.0 MB retained 100 rows/stmt -> 19.0 MB retained ``` No statement in that sweep came within a factor of one and a half of the byte budget, so the entire spread is row count. 3. Confirm it is a floor and not a leak, so the fix is worth a bounded amount and no more. Write 1,000,000 rows at the shipped 1000 per statement and sample as it goes: ``` after batch 1: 82.8 MB after batch 100: 210.9 MB after batch 300: 228.9 MB after batch 600: 234.9 MB after batch 1000: 228.9 MB after 30s idle: 228.9 MB ``` ### After (37f296b4cc) Captured at `39c27ad4b0`. The only changes since are test files, in response to review and to a CI failure; no production file moved, so these numbers still describe the head. `git diff 39c27ad4b0 37f296b4cc --stat` lists only files under `tests/`. #### Case 1: real traffic through a live proxy 1. Same five calls, same prompt, on the PR tree: ``` $ /app/.venv/bin/python -c 'import litellm.proxy.utils as u; print("MARKER_SPEND_LOG_WRITE_BATCH_MAX_ROWS:", getattr(u, "SPEND_LOG_WRITE_BATCH_MAX_ROWS", "ABSENT"))' MARKER_SPEND_LOG_WRITE_BATCH_MAX_ROWS: 100 call 1 -> HTTP 200 id=chatcmpl-EF95CtP3fdvyJh1efVQgpGoAf7XCb content='ok' call 2 -> HTTP 200 id=chatcmpl-EF95DaK95HNHxhfoGRYmLe81qfGQA content='ok' call 3 -> HTTP 200 id=chatcmpl-EF95F0Tcnt1cLCBVWD3b7wuvhfDq1 content='ok' call 4 -> HTTP 200 id=chatcmpl-EF95GFpUfIjbp3hGzSx6x8hHiMw8E content='ok' call 5 -> HTTP 200 id=chatcmpl-EF95HNc5N4yMKpiOv9lMv6FftBs63 content='ok' ``` 2. Wait for the flush and read back what those calls wrote. Same row count, same token counts, same spend to the cent: ``` spend log rows found for those 5 call ids: 5 request_id=chatcmpl-EF95CtP3fdvyJh1efVQgpGoAf7XCb model=openai/gpt-4o-mini spend=0.00000270 total_tokens=15 status=success request_id=chatcmpl-EF95DaK95HNHxhfoGRYmLe81qfGQA model=openai/gpt-4o-mini spend=0.00000270 total_tokens=15 status=success request_id=chatcmpl-EF95F0Tcnt1cLCBVWD3b7wuvhfDq1 model=openai/gpt-4o-mini spend=0.00000270 total_tokens=15 status=success request_id=chatcmpl-EF95GFpUfIjbp3hGzSx6x8hHiMw8E model=openai/gpt-4o-mini spend=0.00000270 total_tokens=15 status=success request_id=chatcmpl-EF95HNc5N4yMKpiOv9lMv6FftBs63 model=openai/gpt-4o-mini spend=0.00000270 total_tokens=15 status=success total real spend for this run: $0.00001350 ``` #### Case 2: the flush at production scale 1. The same three 50,000-row flushes, interleaved with the Before arm: ``` FIX max_rows=100 retained=19.0 MB flush=7.58s all_rows_persisted=True (50000) FIX max_rows=100 retained=23.0 MB flush=6.57s all_rows_persisted=True (50000) FIX max_rows=100 retained=12.9 MB flush=6.29s all_rows_persisted=True (50000) ``` Against the Before arm's 113, 121 and 107 MB, that is a mean of 113.7 MB down to 18.3 MB, or 6.2x. Flush wall time goes from 6.00-6.55s to 6.29-7.58s, so the ranges overlap and the mean cost is about 9%. Every leg on both sides wrote all 50,000 rows, asserted rather than assumed. 2. The same statement-size sweep run three more times as alternating pairs of 100,000 rows, to check the effect is reproducible rather than one lucky sample: ``` 1000 rows/stmt retained [153.0, 153.0, 153.0] MB flush [10.94, 11.07, 10.35] s 100 rows/stmt retained [ 19.0, 23.0, 25.0] MB flush [12.40, 11.17, 12.23] s ``` 3. Mutation check on the new bound. Removing `and end - start < max_rows` from the inner loop: ``` FAILED tests/test_litellm/proxy/db/test_spend_log_batching.py::test_a_row_budget_of_one_yields_one_statement_per_row FAILED tests/test_litellm/proxy/db/test_spend_log_batching.py::test_the_row_budget_splits_a_statement_the_byte_budget_never_would FAILED tests/test_litellm/proxy/db/test_spend_log_batching.py::test_whichever_budget_binds_first_is_the_one_that_splits 3 failed, 14 passed ``` The 14 that still pass are the existing byte-budget tests, which is the check that giving them an explicit non-binding row cap did not quietly stop them measuring bytes. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats - Roughly 9% more flush wall time, from more round trips - Prompt-storing deployments are unaffected; bytes still bind first - Fixes a bounded floor, not a multi-gigabyte engine - Merge BerriAI/litellm-docs#978 first, or `documentation_test_env_keys` fails - Measured on aarch64; the reporter's pods are x86_64
