signal.title: fix(logging): stop billing and logging response reads as LLM calls
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Reading a stored response bills its tokens again - Every read writes a second spend log row - Read/management calls log as normal chat calls - Their spans carry a fake `default-message-value` prompt How it solves it: - Read/management call types are priced at 0 - They report no usage, so no tokens are re-counted - No placeholder chat message is logged for them - Response reads get a `litellm.responses_management` operation name - Vector store and vector store file management call types are classified the same way ## User Flow Before: a developer polling a background response is charged again on every poll, so their spend for one generation keeps growing while they only read it 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `{"model": "gpt-4o", "input": "hello"}` and get back `resp_...` plus an `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.03` header 2. They send GET https://litellm-domain/v1/responses/resp_... to check on it, and get 200 with the same stored output 3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and see two rows for one generation: the create at 6000 tokens, and the read logged as another 6000 token call 4. Polling ten times leaves ten extra rows counting the same tokens, and each read shows up in the same charts as their real chat traffic 5. Deleting a vector store at DELETE https://litellm-domain/v1/vector_stores/vs_... also shows up as a call with a `default-message-value` prompt After: the same polling costs nothing and the read is visibly a management operation, not a generation 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses and get back `resp_...` plus `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.03` 2. They send the same GET https://litellm-domain/v1/responses/resp_... and get 200 with the same stored output, now with no cost header 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the create at 6000 tokens and $0.03, and the read at 0 tokens and $0 4. Polling ten times adds no tokens and no spend, and the reads carry a `litellm.responses_management` operation instead of landing in the chat series 5. The vector store delete is logged with no prompt at all instead of a made-up one ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5602 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Same commands run against a live proxy on localhost:4000 before the fix (at `0a25756e78`) and after it (at `6285192141`). The environment this was captured in cannot reach `api.openai.com`, so the OpenAI base URL pointed at a local server returning a real-shaped Responses object with 4000 input / 2000 output tokens: the double billing is entirely in how the gateway prices the object it reads back, so the numbers below are what a real key produces too. Worth re-running against real OpenAI before merge. ```bash # 1. create a response curl -s -i -X POST localhost:4000/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-4o","input":"hello"}' | grep -iE "^(HTTP|x-litellm-response-cost:)" # 2. read it back curl -s -i localhost:4000/v1/responses/$RID \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" | grep -iE "^(HTTP|x-litellm-response-cost:)" # 3. delete a vector store curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -X DELETE localhost:4000/v1/vector_stores/vs_... \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" # 4. what got billed psql $DATABASE_URL -c 'select call_type, spend, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens from "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" order by "startTime" desc limit 3;' ``` Before, at `0a25756e78`. The read is priced and counted like a generation: ``` POST /v1/responses -> HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost: 0.03 GET /v1/responses/{id} -> HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost: 0.03 DELETE /v1/vector_stores/{id} -> 200 call_type | spend | prompt_tokens | completion_tokens | total_tokens ----------------------+-------+---------------+-------------------+-------------- avector_store_delete | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 aget_responses | 0.03 | 4000 | 2000 | 6000 aresponses | 0.03 | 4000 | 2000 | 6000 ``` The same reading also shows the placeholder prompt: `grep -c default-message-value` over the proxy log for those three requests returns 4 before the fix and 0 after. After, at `6285192141`. The create is unchanged, the read costs nothing and counts nothing: ``` POST /v1/responses -> HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost: 0.03 GET /v1/responses/{id} -> HTTP/1.1 200 OK (no cost header) DELETE /v1/vector_stores/{id} -> 200 call_type | spend | prompt_tokens | completion_tokens | total_tokens ----------------------+-------+---------------+-------------------+-------------- avector_store_delete | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 aget_responses | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 aresponses | 0.03 | 4000 | 2000 | 6000 ``` The `litellm.responses_management` operation name applies to the newer otel payload builders, which this proxy run did not exercise, so that part is covered by unit tests on `resolve_operation` rather than by the log above. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Dashboards counting these reads as spend will now read 0 - Vector store management spans keep their existing operation name - Proof captured against a local provider, not real OpenAI Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/cc8575afe61740bfa53b4548be552350 <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **High Risk** > Changes spend calculation and spend-log token counts for Responses and vector-store management. A wrong origin stamp would leave background jobs unbilled or keep double-charging user polls. > > **Overview** > Stops double-billing stored Responses (and other read/management routes) that replay the original call’s usage. User-facing get/delete/cancel/list and vector-store management now cost **$0**, report **0 tokens**, and no longer log a fake `default-message-value` prompt. > > Adds `NON_INFERENCE_CALL_TYPES` plus `is_unbilled_non_inference_call`, wired into cost calc, standard logging payloads, and spend logs. OTel maps those response routes to `litellm.responses_management` instead of chat. > > **Exception:** the background cost poller stamps `background_response_cost_poll` so its `aget_responses` still bills—queued jobs only expose usage on that poll. Create (`aresponses`) is unchanged. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 120072c72a25ba4ee7c04c21fbf0d15fea972dd8. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: refactor(guardrails): extract the content mapping helper and two payload seams

signal.title: fix(logging): log system prompt when passed as content-block list
signal.text: ## Summary Anthropic's `/v1/messages` API accepts `system` as either a plain string **or** a list of content blocks (e.g. for prompt caching via `cache_control`). The previous `append_system_prompt_messages()` implementation had an `isinstance(..., str)` guard that silently dropped list-form system prompts, so `StandardLoggingPayload.messages` never included the system prompt for any request using the multi-block form. Fixes #36402 ## Root Cause / Motivation ```python # old — silently ignored list-form system if kwargs.get("system") is not None and isinstance(kwargs.get("system"), str): ... ``` Any caller using: ```python litellm.completion( model="claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022", system=[{"type": "text", "text": "You are helpful.", "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}], messages=[...], ) ``` got an empty `messages` field in the logging payload — the system context was invisible to every downstream callback. ## Design Decisions - **Handles both `str` and `list[dict]`** — the same `system_message` dict is prepended with `"content": system`, matching how OpenAI-compatible loggers already represent list-form content. - **New `get_system_prompt_from_kwargs()` helper** checks all three known system kwarg names (`system_instructions`, `instructions`, `system`) in priority order for future-proofing. - **New `system_prompt` field** on `StandardLoggingPayload` surfaces the raw value independently, so callbacks can inspect it without scanning `messages`. - Duplicate-detection logic retained: if the first message already matches the system content, no prepend occurs. ## Changes | File | What changed | |------|-------------| | `litellm/litellm_core_utils/litellm_logging.py` | Added `get_system_prompt_from_kwargs`; replaced old str-only guard in `append_system_prompt_messages` with str+list handling | | `litellm/types/utils.py` | Added `system_prompt: str \| list \| None` to `StandardLoggingPayload` | | `tests/*/create_mock_standard_logging_payload.py` | Added `system_prompt=None` to 3 fixture files to satisfy the new required field | | `tests/logging_callback_tests/test_standard_logging_payload.py` | Added 10 unit tests for string, list, None, empty, duplicate, and str-messages variants | ## Testing - [x] Existing tests pass (no behaviour change for string-form system prompts) - [x] New tests: `TestAppendSystemPromptMessages` — 10 cases covering string, list, None kwargs, empty messages, None messages, duplicate detection, str messages, non-string/non-list values - [x] Manually verified: list-form system now appears in logged `messages` ## Impact Every LiteLLM user who passes `system` as a list of content blocks (common with Anthropic prompt caching) will now see the system prompt reflected in their logging callbacks and observability dashboards.

signal.title: fix(guardrails): take caller identity on /guardrails/apply_guardrail from auth, not the body
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Caller metadata decides identity on `/guardrails/apply_guardrail` - A caller can claim any alias or team id - Guardrails keyed on that metadata can be steered How it solves it: - Authenticated identity is layered over caller metadata - Uses the same sanitizer the in-line request path uses - Non-identity metadata still passes through untouched ## User Flow Before: a guardrail configured to treat one team differently can be talked into it by anyone 1. An admin runs a guardrail that behaves differently for a known key alias or team id, reading it from request metadata 2. A caller sends POST https://litellm-domain/guardrails/apply_guardrail with `"metadata": {"user_api_key_alias": "<the privileged alias>"}` and their own text 3. The response comes back as if the request came from that alias, so text the guardrail would otherwise act on is returned untouched After: the same request is judged on who the caller actually is 1. The caller sends the same POST with the same forged `metadata` 2. The proxy overwrites the identity fields with the ones authentication established for that key 3. The guardrail runs against the real identity, so the forged alias buys nothing, while any other metadata the caller sent still reaches the guardrail ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy on `localhost:4000` at commit `9ce19120fc`, postgres-backed, with a guardrail that skips work for one key alias and a guardrail endpoint that records every payload it receives. The route is admin-only, so the master key is used; its authenticated alias is empty, which is exactly what has to win over the alias the body claims. ``` $ # 1) forged identity in the body $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/guardrails/apply_guardrail \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"guardrail_name":"gg-skip-alias","text":"scan me","metadata":{"user_api_key_alias":"e2e-batch-worker"}}' 200 $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8787/_count # payloads the guardrail received {"records":1} $ # 2) the same call without the forged alias, for contrast 200 {"records":1} ``` Before this change the first call returned `{"records":0}`: the forged alias matched the exemption and the guardrail never ran. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - `request_data` now always carries authenticated metadata - Callers relying on it being absent will see it ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 2a7f02826f811a2bfa4e88201bea5de60d62431a. signal.title: fix(rag): resolve vector store registry credentials in rag query
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - /v1/rag/query never resolves the LiteLLM-managed vector store registry, so a vector store registered with a non-OpenAI provider (and its litellm_params such as api_key and api_base) is still queried against api.openai.com. The standalone /v1/vector_stores/{id}/search endpoint already resolves this via _update_request_data_with_litellm_managed_vector_store_registry; rag_query did not How it solves it: - Reuse the shared resolver in rag_query to load the managed vector store for the requested vector_store_id - Set the resolved custom_llm_provider on retrieval_config so _execute_query_pipeline picks it up (it passes custom_llm_provider to asearch explicitly, so it cannot come through request_data kwargs without a duplicate-argument TypeError) - Forward the resolved litellm_params (minus litellm_credential_name) through request_data so they reach the vector store search ## Relevant issues Closes https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/35599 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile Confidence Score of at least 4/5 before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The regression test test_rag_query_resolves_managed_vector_store_registry fails without this change (asserts the registry provider "bedrock" and aws_region_name reach litellm.aquery) and passes with it. The rag endpoint suite (17 tests) and rag/test_main.py (7 tests) pass. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes - litellm/proxy/rag_endpoints/endpoints.py: resolve managed vector store registry in rag_query - tests/test_litellm/proxy/rag_endpoints/test_rag_endpoints.py: regression test ## QA runbook Run `python -m pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/rag_endpoints/test_rag_endpoints.py tests/test_litellm/rag/test_main.py` ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(spend-tracking): hash raw api keys before persisting to spend logs
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Refused requests could store a raw bearer value in spend logs - The logs page then shows that value under Key Hash - Only `sk-` prefixed keys were hashed before storage How it solves it: - One helper now guards both stored key fields at write time - Anything the gateway has not already hashed gets hashed once - Already-hashed values pass through only when they match the auth-time hash - The master key's stable alias stays readable, the way it was before Also in this PR: the proxy test conftest already snapshots `master_key` and `prisma_client` around every test, so a global one test leaves behind does not reach the next test in the same xdist worker. `llm_router` needed to be on that list too. The PTU rollup reads the running router out of `sys.modules`, so a leftover router lands in its deployment scan and three of its tests pass or fail depending on how xdist happens to split the shard ## User Flow Before: a developer whose bearer token does not start with `sk-` has the whole token stored in spend logs and shown on the logs page 1. The developer sends `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with `Authorization: Bearer <their session token>`, naming a model their key cannot use 2. The proxy refuses it with `400 {"error": {"message": "/chat/completions: Invalid model name passed in model=..."}}` 3. A proxy admin opens `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` and clicks that row, or calls `GET /spend/logs`: the Key Hash field holds the developer's whole session token 4. The same token sits in `LiteLLM_SpendLogs.api_key` and in `metadata.user_api_key` for every row that developer produced, refused or not After: the same calls are stored under a hash, so the logs page and `/spend/logs` return no credential 1. The developer sends the same request 2. The proxy refuses it with the same `400` 3. The admin opens the same page, or calls `GET /spend/logs`, and the Key Hash field holds a 64 character sha256, the same shape virtual key rows have 4. `LiteLLM_SpendLogs.api_key` and `metadata.user_api_key` hold that hash on every row ## Relevant issues Fixes #30670 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both legs run the same flow against a live proxy and the real OpenAI API, and differ only in the commit the proxy booted from. The credential is a non-`sk-` session token handed in through a `custom_auth` hook, which is the documented way to front LiteLLM with your own session credential. Each leg truncates `LiteLLM_SpendLogs`, boots the proxy, sends one refused request and one paid request with that token, then reads the rows back out of Postgres and through `GET /spend/logs`, the endpoint the logs page calls. ### Before, at the merge base `6eacdbfbf09fde6494bd5b93679a48c15eb254de` ``` ### LEG=before ### branch HEAD: 6eacdbfbf09fde6494bd5b93679a48c15eb254de ### spend_tracking_utils.py ACTUALLY LOADED (sha256 of the file on disk): ### 6ff2087c5f2376338c7b44f4c334e5f18ff23023069864b0cbf728df9ffae517 litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/spend_tracking_utils.py ### redaction helper present in that file: ### 56:def _hash_api_key_for_spend_log(api_key: str) -> str: ### port=47219 db=litellm_qa_lit5887_before ### truncated LiteLLM_SpendLogs before this leg ### proxy up after 6s === STEP 1: FAILED request (corp session token, model not in model_list) === $ curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:47219/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer corp-session-<redacted>" \ -d {"model":"gpt-4o-does-not-exist","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]} {"error":{"message":"/chat/completions: Invalid model name passed in model=gpt-4o-does-not-exist. Call `/v1/models` to view available models for your key.","type":"None","param":"None","code":"400",...}} === STEP 2: SUCCESSFUL request (real OpenAI call, real spend) === {"id":"chatcmpl-EFCYD4vgQpL8NwqQD5P6Z5mNk3KBc","created":1787291873,"model":"gpt-4.1-mini","object":"chat.completion",...,"choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"content":"OK","role":"assistant",... ### waiting 20s for spend logs to flush === STEP 3: what landed in LiteLLM_SpendLogs === $ psql -c "SELECT api_key, model, metadata->>'user_api_key' FROM \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\"" model | api_key | metadata_user_api_key -----------------------+-----------------------------------------------+----------------------------------------------- gpt-4o-does-not-exist | corp-session-7f3a9c2e1b8d4a6f5e0c3b7a9d2f4e61 | corp-session-7f3a9c2e1b8d4a6f5e0c3b7a9d2f4e61 openai/gpt-4.1-mini | corp-session-7f3a9c2e1b8d4a6f5e0c3b7a9d2f4e61 | corp-session-7f3a9c2e1b8d4a6f5e0c3b7a9d2f4e61 (2 rows) === STEP 4: does the RAW corp session token appear anywhere in the spend rows? === 2 ^^ number of spend rows containing the RAW token (0 == no leak, >0 == LEAK) === STEP 5: same question through /spend/logs, the endpoint the Admin UI logs page calls === $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:47219/spend/logs -H "Authorization: Bearer <master key>" rows returned: 2 model=openai/gpt-4.1-mini api_key=corp-session-7f3a9c2e1b8d4a6f5e0c3b7a9d2f4e61 model=gpt-4o-does-not-exist api_key=corp-session-7f3a9c2e1b8d4a6f5e0c3b7a9d2f4e61 RAW TOKEN PRESENT IN /spend/logs RESPONSE: True ``` Both rows hold the token exactly as it was sent, in `api_key` and in `metadata.user_api_key`, and `/spend/logs` hands it straight back to the logs page. ### After, at the branch tip `a50590f32454ee845775a04087d6cd42d249f37d` ``` ### LEG=after ### branch HEAD: a50590f32454ee845775a04087d6cd42d249f37d ### spend_tracking_utils.py ACTUALLY LOADED (sha256 of the file on disk): ### d76ac6875abbd3f1e306dfec73b1cbb575e2d41648efdf1797ec8b3053279d38 litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/spend_tracking_utils.py ### redaction helper present in that file: ### 71:def _is_non_secret_key_value(value: str) -> bool: ### 79:def _redact_logged_api_key(value: str | None, *, already_redacted: bool = False) -> str | None: ### port=39481 db=litellm_qa_lit5887_after ### truncated LiteLLM_SpendLogs before this leg ### proxy up after 6s === STEP 1: FAILED request (corp session token, model not in model_list) === $ curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:39481/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer corp-session-<redacted>" \ -d {"model":"gpt-4o-does-not-exist","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]} {"error":{"message":"/chat/completions: Invalid model name passed in model=gpt-4o-does-not-exist. Call `/v1/models` to view available models for your key.","type":"None","param":"None","code":"400",...}} === STEP 2: SUCCESSFUL request (real OpenAI call, real spend) === {"id":"chatcmpl-EFDGCQbFIVouVc83CiPxnPcO7p715","created":1787294600,"model":"gpt-4.1-mini","object":"chat.completion",...,"choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"content":"OK","role":"assistant",... ### waiting 20s for spend logs to flush === STEP 3: what landed in LiteLLM_SpendLogs === $ psql -c "SELECT api_key, model, metadata->>'user_api_key' FROM \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\"" model | api_key | metadata_user_api_key -----------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------ gpt-4o-does-not-exist | bc5a113c99d713ffbafbe6be12b4e815f3cb890972cd7d0175e313d248c65715 | bc5a113c99d713ffbafbe6be12b4e815f3cb890972cd7d0175e313d248c65715 openai/gpt-4.1-mini | bc5a113c99d713ffbafbe6be12b4e815f3cb890972cd7d0175e313d248c65715 | bc5a113c99d713ffbafbe6be12b4e815f3cb890972cd7d0175e313d248c65715 (2 rows) === STEP 4: does the RAW corp session token appear anywhere in the spend rows? === 0 ^^ number of spend rows containing the RAW token (0 == no leak, >0 == LEAK) === STEP 5: same question through /spend/logs, the endpoint the Admin UI logs page calls === $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:39481/spend/logs -H "Authorization: Bearer <master key>" rows returned: 2 model=openai/gpt-4.1-mini api_key=bc5a113c99d713ffbafbe6be12b4e815f3cb890972cd7d0175e313d248c65715 model=gpt-4o-does-not-exist api_key=bc5a113c99d713ffbafbe6be12b4e815f3cb890972cd7d0175e313d248c65715 RAW TOKEN PRESENT IN /spend/logs RESPONSE: False ``` `bc5a113c99d713ffbafbe6be12b4e815f3cb890972cd7d0175e313d248c65715` is `hash_token("corp-session-7f3a9c2e1b8d4a6f5e0c3b7a9d2f4e61")`, so the rows still join and still group per caller, and the value itself is gone. The refused request is stored the same way as the paid one. Both legs used a throwaway token that never existed anywhere real. ### Master-key rows keep their readable alias Master-key auth stamps the stable alias `litellm_proxy_master_key` instead of the raw key, so those spend rows carry a readable identifier rather than a credential. The first version of this change did not recognize that alias and hashed it, which broke continuity with every master-key row written before the change. Same flow as above, default auth this time (no `custom_auth`), one real OpenAI call authenticated with the master key. Before the alias fix, at `c7b34da079e962d006e3b109739203703fa152f6`: ``` model | api_key | metadata_user_api_key ---------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------ openai/gpt-4.1-mini | 05315140fffb69fbf877806e62016cf1e0fb2669ac12e060a13915f0942ee017 | 05315140fffb69fbf877806e62016cf1e0fb2669ac12e060a13915f0942ee017 (1 row) ``` At the tip `a50590f32454ee845775a04087d6cd42d249f37d`: ``` model | api_key | metadata_user_api_key ---------------------+--------------------------+-------------------------- openai/gpt-4.1-mini | litellm_proxy_master_key | litellm_proxy_master_key (1 row) ``` `05315140fffb69fbf877806e62016cf1e0fb2669ac12e060a13915f0942ee017` is the sha256 of the alias itself. Neither leg stores the raw master key: the row count matching it is 0 in both. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - This guards spend log rows, not the proxy's own stdout or stderr. The other log sinks raised in the comments above sit on separate code paths and are tracked separately, so they stay out of scope here - The read side of `/spend/logs` still branches on `api_key.startswith("sk-")` when you filter by key, so filtering by a non-`sk-` credential still needs the raw value. That is the same behavior as before this PR and no row is stored differently because of it ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: perf(ci): cache uv dependencies in the lint job
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `lint` is the slowest required check, 9 of last 10 staging PRs - It reinstalls every dependency from scratch on every run - That one step is 2.8 min of a 9.5 min p50 job How it solves it: - Cache `~/.cache/uv` and `.venv` keyed on `uv.lock` - Same block `_test-unit-base.yml` already uses - Own `lint` key namespace, since group sets differ ## User Flow No end-user behavior changes. This is CI-only: it changes how long a required check takes, not what it reports. Contributors see the same pass/fail on the same rules, sooner. ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The change is a CI wall-clock change, so the measurement is the workflow run itself. `test-linting.yml` triggers only on `pull_request`, so the After side is this PR's own run and lands once it completes. ### Before (e17988f4fe) #### Slowest required check, last 10 merged staging PRs 1. Query the ruleset for the required contexts, then time every check run on each PR head: ``` gh api repos/BerriAI/litellm/rules/branches/litellm_internal_staging \ --jq '.[] | select(.type=="required_status_checks") | .parameters.required_status_checks[].context' > req.txt for SHA in $(gh pr list -R BerriAI/litellm --base litellm_internal_staging --state merged --limit 10 --json headRefOid --jq '.[].headRefOid'); do gh api "repos/BerriAI/litellm/commits/$SHA/check-runs?per_page=100" --paginate \ --jq '.check_runs[] | select(.conclusion=="success" or .conclusion=="failure") | [((((.completed_at|fromdateiso8601)-(.started_at|fromdateiso8601))/60)*10|round/10), .name] | @tsv' \ | awk -F'\t' 'NR==FNR{r[$0];next} $2 in r' req.txt - | sort -rn | head -1 done ``` 2. Output, minutes and check name: ``` 9.6 lint 8.9 lint 10 lint 9.2 lint 9.1 lint 9.7 lint 8.5 proxy-endpoints / Run tests 10 lint 9.9 lint 9.4 lint ``` #### Where the time goes inside lint 1. Step durations for the most recent staging `lint` run: ``` gh api "repos/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/32439641315/jobs?per_page=100" \ --jq '.jobs[] | select(.name=="lint") | .steps[] | select(.conclusion!=null) | [((((.completed_at|fromdateiso8601)-(.started_at|fromdateiso8601))/60)*10|round/10), .name] | @tsv' | sort -rn | head -4 ``` 2. signal.title: fix(exceptions): distinguish non-retryable insufficient_quota from transient RateLimitError
signal.text: ## Relevant issues <!-- e.g., "Fixes #000" --> ## Linear ticket <!-- if you are an internal contributor, add "Resolves " followed by the Linear ticket e.g., "Resolves LIT-1234" to link the Linear ticket to the GitHub PR. If you don't have one, leave the section blank rather than guessing --> ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [X] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [X] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The reproduction uses a dedicated OpenAI project with a $1/month hard budget cap, burned to the cap with real `litellm.completion` calls, so both captures below are live API responses — no mocks, no monkeypatching. The raw provider rejection, captured with a direct curl against `https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions`: ``` { "error": { "message": "You exceeded your current quota, please check your plan and billing details. For more information on this error, read the docs: https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/error-codes/api-errors.", "type": "insufficient_quota", "param": null, "code": "insufficient_quota" } } HTTP_STATUS: 429 ``` **Before (merge-base `3d63edaa6d2ed5f74d7762a07b058e678226907b`)** — the quota error surfaces as a plain `RateLimitError` with `type: throttling_error`, indistinguishable from a transient 429: ``` commit: 3d63edaa6d2ed5f74d7762a07b058e678226907b type(exc).__name__: RateLimitError isinstance(exc, litellm.RateLimitError): True exc.status_code: 429 exc.code: 429 exc.type: throttling_error --- str(exc) verbatim --- litellm.RateLimitError: RateLimitError: OpenAIException - You exceeded your current quota, please check your plan and billing details. For more information on this error, read the docs: https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/error-codes/api-errors. ``` **After (PR head `7fc261308e654c150b298b786223822112797318`)** — the same probe on the same exhausted key now raises `InsufficientQuotaError` with `code`/`type == insufficient_quota`, and it is **still caught by `except litellm.RateLimitError`** (backwards compatibility, demonstrated live): ``` commit: 7fc261308e654c150b298b786223822112797318 type(exc).__name__: InsufficientQuotaError isinstance(exc, litellm.RateLimitError): True exc.status_code: 429 exc.code: insufficient_quota exc.type: insufficient_quota --- str(exc) verbatim --- litellm.InsufficientQuotaError: litellm.RateLimitError: RateLimitError: OpenAIException - You exceeded your current quota, please check your plan and billing details. For more information on this error, read the docs: https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/error-codes/api-errors. ``` Probe command, identical for both captures except the checked-out commit: ```python import litellm try: litellm.completion(model="gpt-5.6", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say OK."}], max_tokens=16, api_key=REPRO_KEY, num_retries=0) except Exception as exc: print(type(exc).__name__, isinstance(exc, litellm.RateLimitError), getattr(exc, "code", None)) raise ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes **What / why:** When an OpenAI key has no remaining quota (`code: "insufficient_quota"` — a billing state), LiteLLM mapped it to the same `litellm.RateLimitError` used for transient rate-limit 429s, because the mapping matches the `429` token in the error string before the error code is consulted. Retry policies key on `RateLimitError` as retryable, so callers retry a condition that retrying cannot fix (see #14547, #12497 for users hitting this in the wild). This adds an `InsufficientQuotaError(RateLimitError)` subtype and detects the quota case in `_map_openai_exception` **before** the generic rate-limit branch. It carries `code`/`type == "insufficient_quota"` so callers can also branch on the attribute. **Backwards compatible:** existing `except RateLimitError` handlers still catch it (it subclasses `RateLimitError`); retry policies that want to skip billing errors can now exclude the subtype. **Scope, deliberately narrow:** detection keys on OpenAI's `insufficient_quota` code only. Other providers' "quota" 429s (e.g. Vertex's refilling per-minute quotas) are untouched — those are genuinely transient and should stay retryable. Happy to extend to other providers' billing-state codes with maintainer input. **Tests:** mocked tests added in `tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_exception_mapping_utils.py` — quota string → `InsufficientQuotaError`; isinstance `RateLimitError` (backwards compat); transient 429 still maps to plain `RateLimitError`; attributes set. File passes 64/64. **Disclosure:** built with AI assistance (my two-agent Claude workflow — Claude Code implemented against my written spec). The issue analysis, scope decisions, and line-by-line review are mine.

signal.title: fix(stream_chunk_builder): guard empty choices and missing role in build_base_response
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `build_base_response()` reads `first_chunk_with_choices["choices"][0]["delta"]["role"]` with no bounds check and no key check - Empty `choices` array raises `IndexError`; a `delta` without `role` raises `KeyError` - Both surface as `litellm.APIError: Error building chunks for logging/streaming usage calculation`, which `async_data_generator()` writes into the SSE stream — so the client's response is **truncated mid-stream with no `data: [DONE]`**, and the request is **missing from SpendLogs** - Seen in production on Anthropic/Claude streaming How it solves it: - Fall back to `None` instead of the first chunk, so an all-empty-`choices` stream no longer indexes into `[]` - Guard the array length and use `.get("delta", {}).get("role")` - Default to `"assistant"`, the only role a completion response can carry - No behaviour change for well-formed chunks The loop immediately below the patched line already guards with `len(chunk["choices"]) > 0`; this line was simply missed. Note this is **not** fixed by #34382 / #32203: those handle a *missing* `choices` key (`KeyError('choices')`, #32051 / #32951) by switching to `c.get("choices")`. Here `choices` is present but empty, so `.get()` returns `[]`, `next()` skips it, and the default fallback still indexes out of range. Neither PR touches the `["choices"][0]` access. ## Relevant issues Fixes #37780 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `litellm/litellm_core_utils/streaming_chunk_builder_utils.py`: ```python first_chunk_with_choices = next((c for c in chunks if c.get("choices")), None) role: str = "assistant" if first_chunk_with_choices is not None: _choices = first_chunk_with_choices["choices"] if len(_choices) > 0: role = _choices[0].get("delta", {}).get("role") or "assistant" ``` Tests added to `tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_streaming_chunk_builder_utils.py` cover all-empty-`choices`, usage-only frames, `delta` without `role`, and `delta` as `{}`, plus a regression case asserting normal multi-chunk assembly keeps its role and `finish_reason`. Verified the tests fail without the fix (2 × `IndexError`, 2 × `KeyError` at the patched line) and pass with it; the full test file is green at 34 passed.

signal.title: [Bug]: stream_chunk_builder raises IndexError/KeyError in build_base_response, truncating client SSE stream and skipping SpendLogs
signal.text: ### What happened? `ChunkProcessor.build_base_response()` reads the assistant role without guarding either the `choices` array bounds or the presence of a `role` key: ```python # litellm/litellm_core_utils/streaming_chunk_builder_utils.py first_chunk_with_choices: Final = next((c for c in chunks if c.get("choices")), chunk) role: Final = first_chunk_with_choices["choices"][0]["delta"]["role"] ``` Two distinct failures follow: 1. **`IndexError: list index out of range`** — when no chunk carries a non-empty `choices` array, `next()` returns its default (the *first* chunk), whose `choices` is `[]`. The `[0]` access then goes out of bounds. 2. **`KeyError: 'role'`** — when the first choice's `delta` omits `role` or is `{}`. Either one propagates out of `stream_chunk_builder()` as: ``` litellm.APIError: Error building chunks for logging/streaming usage calculation ``` `proxy_server.async_data_generator()` catches it and writes it into the response stream: ```python error_returned = json.dumps({"error": proxy_exception.to_dict()}) yield f"data: {error_returned}\n\n" ``` Control then goes straight to `finally`, so **`data: [DONE]` is never emitted**. Note the loop directly below the offending line already guards correctly with `len(chunk["choices"]) > 0`, so this looks like a simple omission rather than intent. ### Impact This is not only a logging-path bug. Two user-visible consequences: - **The client's stream is truncated.** The user has already received part of the answer, then the stream stops and an error frame arrives with no `[DONE]`. HTTP status is still 200, because SSE headers are flushed before the failure — so this does not show up as a 5xx in proxy access logs. - **The request is missing from SpendLogs**, so it is never billed. In our production proxy this hit Anthropic/Claude streaming intermittently — a handful of requests per day across a week. Successful responses in the same second were 19KB–339KB; the failing ones returned only ~360 bytes (just the error frame) after 8–38s. ### Relevant log output ```shell LiteLLM:ERROR: main.py:7815 - litellm.main.py::stream_chunk_builder() - Exception occurred - list index out of range Traceback (most recent call last): File "litellm/litellm_core_utils/streaming_handler.py", line 2147, in __anext__ raise StopAsyncIteration StopAsyncIteration During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred: Traceback (most recent call last): File "litellm/main.py", line 7561, in stream_chunk_builder response = processor.build_base_response(chunks) File "litellm/litellm_core_utils/streaming_chunk_builder_utils.py", line 123, in build_base_response role = first_chunk_with_choices["choices"][0]["delta"]["role"] ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^ IndexError: list index out of range LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: proxy_server.py:7081 - litellm.proxy.proxy_server.async_data_generator(): Exception occured - litellm.APIError: Error building chunks for logging/streaming usage calculation ``` ### Reproduction ```python from litellm.litellm_core_utils.streaming_chunk_builder_utils import ChunkProcessor def mk(choices, **kw): d = {"id": "c1", "object": "chat.completion.chunk", "created": 1, "model": "claude-opus-4-8", "choices": choices} d.update(kw) return d cases = { "all-empty-choices": [mk([]), mk([])], "usage-only frames": [mk([], usage={"prompt_tokens": 10}), mk([], usage={"completion_tokens": 0})], "delta without role": [mk([{"index": 0, "delta": {"content": "Hi"}, "finish_reason": None}])], "delta empty dict": [mk([{"index": 0, "delta": {}, "finish_reason": None}])], } for name, chunks in cases.items(): try: ChunkProcessor(chunks=list(chunks)).build_base_response(list(chunks)) print(f"[ok] {name}") except Exception as e: print(f"[fail] {name} -> {type(e).__name__}: {e}") ``` Output on v1.88.1 and on current `litellm_internal_staging`: ``` [fail] all-empty-choices -> IndexError: list index out of range [fail] usage-only frames -> IndexError: list index out of range [fail] delta without role -> KeyError: 'role' [fail] delta empty dict -> KeyError: 'role' ``` ### Relation to existing issues #32051 and #32951 report `KeyError('choices')` — a *missing* `choices` key. #34382 and #32203 address that by switching to `c.get("choices")`. Those changes do not fix this report: here `choices` is **present but empty**, so `.get("choices")` returns `[]` (falsy), `next()` skips it, and the default fallback lands on a chunk that still indexes out of range. Neither PR touches the `["choices"][0]` access itself. ### Are you a ML Ops Team? No ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.88.1, and the same code is present unchanged on `litellm_internal_staging` as of 2026-08-21 (latest release v1.97.0). ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: chore(typing): clear 1.5k basedpyright Any errors across 54 files
signal.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - reportAny and reportExplicitAny keep drifting toward their basedpyright ceilings - 54 source files carried 2,138 Any errors between them - Stale budget headroom lets fresh Any land unreviewed How it solves it: - Real types at each Any source, no casts, ignores, or suppressions - TypedDicts and typed accessors replace untyped JSON and dict payloads - Ratchets budgets down: basedpyright -1,941, ruff-strict -164, LIT -129 - Adds a regression test for the retyped GDC credential boundary ## User Flow Nothing here is broken today and nothing changes for the user. This is a typing-only refactor, so both sides are recorded to show the flow is step for step identical Before: a developer using the gateway gets exactly the responses they expect 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "anthropic-haiku-4-5"` and a short prompt, and get 200 with the assistant message plus real prompt and completion token counts 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the same model and prompt, and get 200 with an Anthropic-shaped `content` block and a `usage` object 3. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `"model": "gpt-5-mini"`, and get 200 with an `output` array and a `usage` object 4. They send the same chat completion again with `"stream": true`, and get SSE `data:` chunks whose deltas assemble into the full reply, ending with a usage-carrying chunk and `[DONE]` 5. They send GET https://litellm-domain/v1/models and see both configured model ids After: identical, step for step 1. Same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions, same 200 with the assistant message and the same token-count fields 2. Same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages, same 200 with the same Anthropic-shaped `content` block and `usage` object 3. Same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses, same 200 with the same `output` array and `usage` object 4. Same streaming request, same SSE chunk sequence, same assembled reply, same trailing usage chunk 5. Same GET https://litellm-domain/v1/models, same two model ids ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Two proofs: a live proxy on both commits showing the user-visible behavior is unchanged, and the whole-tree basedpyright measurement showing the Any counts actually dropped Both proxies ran from the same checkout, on the same interpreter, with the same config and real Anthropic and OpenAI keys, so the money spent is real and the only difference between the runs is the diff in this PR ```yaml # qa_config.yaml model_list: - model_name: anthropic-haiku-4-5 litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY - model_name: gpt-5-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-5-mini api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` ```bash PORT=39631 # the before run, the after run used 39117 python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config qa_config.yaml --port "$PORT" H=(-H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json") curl -s "${H[@]}" "http://localhost:$PORT/v1/chat/completions" \ -d '{"model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: pong"}],"max_tokens":16}' curl -s "${H[@]}" "http://localhost:$PORT/v1/messages" \ -d '{"model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: pong"}],"max_tokens":16}' curl -s "${H[@]}" "http://localhost:$PORT/v1/responses" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-5-mini","input":"Reply with exactly: pong"}' curl -s -N "${H[@]}" "http://localhost:$PORT/v1/chat/completions" \ -d '{"model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Count: one two three"}],"max_tokens":32,"stream":true,"stream_options":{"include_usage":true}}' curl -s "${H[@]}" "http://localhost:$PORT/v1/models" ``` Response bodies below are trimmed to the fields under test, and the streaming case is reported as its assembled deltas plus the chunk count ### Before (5290150a05) ``` --- POST /v1/chat/completions --- {"model": "anthropic-haiku-4-5", "content": "pong", "finish_reason": "stop", "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 13, "completion_tokens": 5, "total_tokens": 18}} --- POST /v1/messages --- {"type": "message", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "pong"}], "stop_reason": "end_turn", "usage": {"input_tokens": 13, "output_tokens": 5, "service_tier": "standard"}} --- POST /v1/responses --- {"object": "response", "status": "completed", "model": "gpt-5-mini", "output_text": ["pong"], "usage": {"input_tokens": 11, "output_tokens": 66, "total_tokens": 77}} --- POST /v1/chat/completions (stream=true) --- {"sse_chunks": 4, "assembled_content": "one, two, three

That's a count of **3**.", "finish_reason": "stop", "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 12, "completion_tokens": 17, "total_tokens": 29}} --- GET /v1/models --- ["anthropic-haiku-4-5", "gpt-5-mini"] ``` ### After (64e993773d) ``` --- POST /v1/chat/completions --- {"model": "anthropic-haiku-4-5", "content": "pong", "finish_reason": "stop", "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 13, "completion_tokens": 5, "total_tokens": 18}} --- POST /v1/messages --- {"type": "message", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "pong"}], "stop_reason": "end_turn", "usage": {"input_tokens": 13, "output_tokens": 5, "service_tier": "standard"}} --- POST /v1/responses --- {"object": "response", "status": "completed", "model": "gpt-5-mini", "output_text": ["pong"], "usage": {"input_tokens": 11, "output_tokens": 55, "total_tokens": 66}} --- POST /v1/chat/completions (stream=true) --- {"sse_chunks": 4, "assembled_content": "one, two, three

(That's a count of 3 items.)", "finish_reason": "stop", "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 12, "completion_tokens": 20, "total_tokens": 32}} --- GET /v1/models --- ["anthropic-haiku-4-5", "gpt-5-mini"] ``` Every field is identical except the model's own free text and its token counts, which vary per sampling call Whole-tree basedpyright before and after, both runs from the same checkout and the same interpreter so the environment cannot skew the delta, counting severity=error diagnostics in-tree: ``` rule before after delta reportAny 13,448 12,266 -1,182 reportExplicitAny 4,484 4,209 -275 reportUnknownMemberType 27,923 27,788 -135 reportUnknownVariableType 21,973 21,857 -116 reportUnknownParameterType 13,585 13,506 -79 reportUnknownArgumentType 38,146 38,080 -66 reportMissingTypeArgument 10,879 10,822 -57 reportMissingParameterType 3,775 3,752 -23 reportUnusedVariable 146 142 -4 reportUnnecessaryCast 116 115 -1 reportUnnecessaryComparison 699 698 -1 reportUnnecessaryIsInstance 852 851 -1 reportUnusedImport 481 480 -1 all rules combined 143,510 141,569 -1,941 ``` That is every rule whose count moved. No basedpyright rule increased, repo-wide or in any individual file: of the 48 budgeted rules 13 dropped and the other 35 are unchanged, so nothing was traded away to get the Any counts down `make lint-budget-update` output confirming the fixes are real and the ceilings now hold them, with the basedpyright figure landing on the same 1,941 the measurement above found: ``` Ratcheted strict-rule limits down by 164 violations this branch fixed Ratcheted LIT-rule limits down by 129 violations this branch fixed Ratcheted basedpyright limits down by 1941 errors this branch fixed across 48 rules ``` `from litellm import *` import safety and the circular import check both pass, and `make check` is green ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ## Changes Typing-only changes across 54 files, chosen by reportAny/reportExplicitAny density. No runtime behavior changes: annotations, TYPE_CHECKING imports, TypedDicts, Protocols, and typed accessors that pay the untyped-to-typed crossing once at a boundary instead of leaking Any through every caller Four root causes account for most of the diff. Untyped prisma reads now go through small typed table Protocols so the Any stops at the query, as in `toolset_db.py`, `oauth2_flow_backfill.py`, and the repositories. `dict[str, Any]` payloads became local TypedDicts: guardrail request and response bodies, opik payload builders, agent registry entries, audit log records. Streaming and logging callbacks that took `Any` now take the concrete chunk and logging types they already imported, as in `streaming_handler.py`, `custom_logger.py`, and `background_streaming.py`. Genuinely duck-typed SDK objects are reached through 3-argument `getattr` with a `Callable` annotation instead of an `Any`-typed attribute read, which keeps the existing `hasattr`-style semantics exactly Forbidden constructs were not used anywhere in the diff: no `cast()`, no `# type: ignore`, no `# noqa`, no suppression comments, no new `Any` annotations. Diagnostics that could not be fixed without one of those were left in place rather than hidden, which is why roughly 770 target errors remain in the touched files, mostly the irreducible one-flag-per-seam residue where an upstream source still hands back Any Budget files are ratcheted by `make lint-budget-update` so the cleared headroom cannot silently grow back One regression test is added, in `tests/test_litellm/llms/gdc/chat/test_gdc_chat_transformation.py`: the GDC config used to reach `with_gdch_audience` off an `Any`-typed credential, so a credential object missing that method failed deep inside google-auth with an opaque error. The typed accessor now raises a named `AttributeError` at the boundary, and the test pins it. Mutation-checked: deleting the raise makes the test fail ## Caveats (if any) - `litellm/llms/nvidia_riva/audio_transcription/audio_utils.py` and the four async visitor methods in `custom_code/sandbox.py` are deliberately left on `Any`. Both sit right against an untyped third-party surface: numpy's overloads reject any stand-in for a real `ndarray`, and RestrictedPython's `RestrictingNodeTransformer` denies every async node, so basedpyright infers those base handlers as returning `None` and a subclass that permits the node reads as an incompatible override. Typing them anyway traded 53 Any errors for 12 new hard type errors, so they were left alone rather than papered over with a suppression ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(cli): bound every keychain call and name an oversized credential
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Keychain reads and deletes had no timeout - An unanswered keychain prompt hung `lite` forever - Windows caps a credential at 2560 bytes - Oversized credentials were reported as "no keychain" How it solves it: - Every keychain call now runs under the 5s bound - A timed-out read reports the keychain unreachable - A timed-out delete warns the credential survives - An oversized payload gets its own honest message ## User Flow Before: a user on a machine whose keychain asks before handing anything over gets a `lite` that never comes back 1. They run `lite whoami` on a box where the OS keychain wants an unlock or an allow-this-app answer first 2. No prompt is answered, so the command sits there with no output and no error, and has to be killed 3. They run `lite login` on Windows while on a team with a dozen or so models, and it prints "No OS keychain available", so they go looking for a broken keychain that is working fine 4. The key lands in `~/.litellm/token.json` and they are not told why After: the same commands come back within about five seconds and say what actually happened 1. They run `lite whoami` on the same box and it returns in roughly five seconds with "Signed in, but the credential cannot be read", plus a line telling them to unlock the keychain or run `lite login` again 2. They run `lite logout` while the keychain is still unanswered and it says the credential may still be in the keychain, so a second logout once it is unlocked finishes the job 3. They run `lite login` on Windows on that same team and it says the credential is too large for the OS keychain and names the owner-only file it went to instead 4. Either way the file stays `0600` and holds no more than it did before ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: a real GNOME Secret Service on Linux, a proxy on `http://127.0.0.1:4000`, and `$AUDIT_ENV` standing in for the `HOME`, `PYTHONPATH` and `PYTHON_KEYRING_BACKEND` prefix that selects the backend under test. Case 2 stands in for the Windows Credential Manager limit, which cannot be exercised from a Linux box: the backend refuses a payload over 2560 UTF-16 bytes exactly as `CredWrite` does. Secret values are redacted throughout. Full transcript, including the happy path re-run at the tip (`whoami`, `models list` against the live proxy, `logout` clearing both stores), is in the session ### Before (66a6a0970690a3650b0be2bcf87b31042f124cf8) #### Unbounded read 1. Store a credential through the real save path, then point at a backend whose `get_password` sleeps 600s ``` $ timeout 30s env $AUDIT_ENV PYTHON_KEYRING_BACKEND=blocking_read_keyring_backend.Keyring lite --base-url http://127.0.0.1:4000 whoami real 30.010 [exit 124] ``` 2. Nothing is printed, and the 30s timeout is what ends it, not the CLI #### Oversized credential 1. Save a real record whose keychain payload crosses 2560 UTF-16 bytes ``` $ env $AUDIT_ENV PYTHON_KEYRING_BACKEND=oversized_keyring_backend.Keyring python proof_support.py save-oversize KeyringUnreachable No OS keychain available. Credential stored in .../.litellm/token.json (owner-only). ``` 2. The keychain is available; the user is told otherwise ``` $ env $AUDIT_ENV python proof_support.py file-summary token.json mode=0600 key=present length=1603 ``` ### After (33b9af5248263875979d71d4dcfb62ecaf634ef4) #### Unbounded read 1. Same stored credential, same 600s backend ``` $ timeout 30s env $AUDIT_ENV PYTHON_KEYRING_BACKEND=blocking_read_keyring_backend.Keyring lite --base-url http://127.0.0.1:4000 whoami Signed in, but the credential cannot be read User Email: proof@example.invalid User ID: proof-user User Role: Internal User Token age: 0.0 hours Your credential is in your OS keychain, which could not be read. Unlock it, or run 'lite login' to start over. real 7.914 [exit 0] ``` 2. It returns on its own, and says which store it could not reach #### Oversized credential 1. Same record, same backend ``` $ env $AUDIT_ENV PYTHON_KEYRING_BACKEND=oversized_keyring_backend.Keyring python proof_support.py save-oversize SecretTooLarge Your credential is too large for the OS keychain, so it was stored in .../.litellm/token.json (owner-only) instead. ``` 2. The fallback file is unchanged, the reason is now the real one ``` $ env $AUDIT_ENV python proof_support.py file-summary token.json mode=0600 key=present length=1603 ``` Linux screen recording of the keychain flows, happy path and the degraded-keychain cases, is in the Slack thread: https://berriaillm.slack.com/archives/D0BE7TV8KSQ/p1787276229358619?thread_ts=1787276229.358619&cid=D0BE7TV8KSQ ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Windows and macOS were not executed, no such host - Windows oversize case verified through an equivalent Linux backend - Oversized credentials still fall back to the file, not chunked - Shrinking the payload below the Windows cap is follow-up work ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/d047369df67f494da3959ab632762b30 Requested by: @mateo-berri

signal.title: feat(together_ai): capability baseline, reasoning controls, and a current model map
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Unmapped Together models silently lost tool calling - Structured outputs dropped alongside them - Reasoning controls never reached any Together model - Mapped per-model rates were shadowed by parameter-count buckets - Cache hits with no published discount billed as free - Reasoning tokens billed twice on some usage shapes - Calls went to the legacy api.together.xyz host How it solves it: - Provider-level capability baseline, like fireworks_ai has - Reasoning, logprobs and max_tokens mapped to Together's shapes - Size buckets now price only what the map does not - A cache hit falls back to the standard input rate - Overlapping completion token details no longer double-count - Catalog refreshed, with cached-input rates - Default base URL is now the documented api.together.ai ## User Flow Before: a developer building an agent on a model Together launched this week gets no tool calls back, cannot turn thinking off, and sees the wrong spend 1. They add `together_ai/moonshotai/Kimi-K3` to their proxy config and restart 2. They send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with that model, a `tools` array holding one `get_weather` function, and "What is the weather in Paris? Use the tool." 3. The reply is prose, "I don't have access to a weather tool or any real-time data sources", with no `tool_calls` array, so their agent loop has nothing to execute 4. On a proxy without `drop_params` the same request fails outright with 500 `together_ai does not support parameters: ['tools']` 5. They switch to `together_ai/Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B` and send `"reasoning_effort": "none"` to skip thinking on a simple question; the answer still arrives behind 869 characters of chain of thought, and they pay for those tokens 6. They send a 4.7k-token prompt to Kimi K3 twice and read the `x-litellm-response-cost` response header: it is empty both times, so the calls land in their dashboard at zero spend 7. They repeat the same prompt against `together_ai/meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo` and the header reads `0.0042876` every time, which is $0.90 per 1M tokens rather than the $1.04 Together publishes, and the response `usage` carries no cached-token count for their cache-hit dashboard 8. They stream from `together_ai/Qwen/Qwen3.7-Plus`, which returns 140 completion tokens, and the spend recorded for that turn reflects 274 output tokens After: the same requests return tool calls, thinking is controllable, and the spend numbers match Together's published rates 1. They add `together_ai/moonshotai/Kimi-K3` to their proxy config and restart 2. They send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with that model, a `tools` array holding one `get_weather` function, and "What is the weather in Paris? Use the tool." 3. The reply comes back with `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` and a `tool_calls` array naming `get_weather` with `{"location": "Paris"}`, so the agent loop runs 4. `"response_format": {"type": "json_schema", ...}` on the same model returns schema-shaped JSON instead of a 500 5. On `together_ai/Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B`, `"reasoning_effort": "none"` returns the answer with no chain of thought at all, and the same request without it still thinks 6. They send a 4.7k-token prompt to Kimi K3 twice: the first call's `x-litellm-response-cost` reads `0.0141912` and the second, hitting Together's warm prefix, reads `0.0015444`, a 9x drop that shows up in their dashboard 7. The same prompt against Llama 3.3 70B Instruct Turbo reads `0.00495456`, matching Together's published $1.04 per 1M, and the response `usage` now reports `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` so their cache-hit dashboard is no longer stuck at zero 8. Streaming from `together_ai/Qwen/Qwen3.7-Plus` charges the 140 completion tokens the model actually produced ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both sides ran against the same live Together AI account, one proxy per side, with `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True` so the bundled map is the one under test. `qa_config.yaml`: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: kimi-k3 litellm_params: model: together_ai/moonshotai/Kimi-K3 api_key: os.environ/TOGETHER_API_KEY - model_name: llama-3.3-70b litellm_params: model: together_ai/meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo api_key: os.environ/TOGETHER_API_KEY - model_name: qwen3.5-9b litellm_params: model: together_ai/Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B api_key: os.environ/TOGETHER_API_KEY litellm_settings: drop_params: True telemetry: False general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` ```bash LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config qa_config.yaml --port 4010 ``` Cases 3 and 4 send a 4.7k-token prefix twice so Together's automatic prefix cache can warm between calls. Cache hits are best-effort, so which call lands warm varies. ### Before (66a89f5a6e) #### Tool calling on a model the cost map does not know 1. `curl -sS localhost:4010/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @case1_tools.json | jq -c '{finish_reason: .choices[0].finish_reason, tool_calls: .choices[0].message.tool_calls, content_head: (.choices[0].message.content // "" | .[0:80])}'` 2. `{"finish_reason":"stop","tool_calls":null,"content_head":"I don't have access to a weather tool or any real-time data sources, so I'm unab"}` #### Turning thinking off on a hybrid model 1. `curl -sS localhost:4010/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"qwen3.5-9b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Is 9.11 bigger than 9.9? Answer in one short sentence."}],"reasoning_effort":"none","max_tokens":600}' | jq -c '{reasoning_chars: (.choices[0].message.reasoning_content // "" | length), content_head: (.choices[0].message.content // "" | .[0:60])}'` 2. `{"reasoning_chars":869,"content_head":"No, 9.11 is smaller than 9.9."}` #### Cost and cached input on Kimi K3 1. `for i in 1 2; do curl -sS -D h.txt localhost:4010/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @case3_cache.json | jq -c .usage; grep -i '^x-litellm-response-cost:' h.txt; done` 2. call 1 (cold): `x-litellm-response-cost:` (empty) with `{"completion_tokens":8,"prompt_tokens":4748,"total_tokens":4756,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":64}}` 3. call 2 (warm): `x-litellm-response-cost:` (empty) with `{"completion_tokens":8,"prompt_tokens":4748,"total_tokens":4756,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":4748}}` #### Published rate and flat cached tokens on Llama 3.3 70B 1. `for i in 1 2; do curl -sS -D h.txt localhost:4010/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @case4_flat.json | jq -c '{usage, cached_via_details: .usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens}'; grep -i '^x-litellm-response-cost:' h.txt; done` 2. call 1: `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0042876` with `{"usage":{"completion_tokens":2,"prompt_tokens":4762,"total_tokens":4764,"cached_tokens":0},"cached_via_details":null}` 3. call 2: `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0042876` with `{"usage":{"completion_tokens":2,"prompt_tokens":4762,"total_tokens":4764,"cached_tokens":0},"cached_via_details":null}` ### After (b94e4a74d5) #### Tool calling on a model the cost map does not know 1. `curl -sS localhost:4010/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @case1_tools.json | jq -c '{finish_reason: .choices[0].finish_reason, tool_calls: .choices[0].message.tool_calls, content_head: (.choices[0].message.content // "" | .[0:80])}'` 2. `{"finish_reason":"tool_calls","tool_calls":[{"function":{"arguments":"{\"location\":\"Paris\"}","name":"get_weather"},"id":"get_weather_0","type":"function"}],"content_head":"I'll check the current weather in Paris for you."}` #### Turning thinking off on a hybrid model 1. `curl -sS localhost:4010/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"qwen3.5-9b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Is 9.11 bigger than 9.9? Answer in one short sentence."}],"reasoning_effort":"none","max_tokens":600}' | jq -c '{reasoning_chars: (.choices[0].message.reasoning_content // "" | length), content_head: (.choices[0].message.content // "" | .[0:60])}'` 2. `{"reasoning_chars":0,"content_head":"No, 9.9 is bigger than 9.11."}` #### Cost and cached input on Kimi K3 1. `for i in 1 2; do curl -sS -D h.txt localhost:4010/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @case3_cache.json | jq -c .usage; grep -i '^x-litellm-response-cost:' h.txt; done` 2. call 1 (cold): `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.014191200000000001` with `{"completion_tokens":8,"prompt_tokens":4748,"total_tokens":4756,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":64}}` 3. call 2 (warm): `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0015444` with `{"completion_tokens":8,"prompt_tokens":4748,"total_tokens":4756,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":4748}}` #### Published rate and flat cached tokens on Llama 3.3 70B 1. `for i in 1 2; do curl -sS -D h.txt localhost:4010/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @case4_flat.json | jq -c '{usage, cached_via_details: .usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens}'; grep -i '^x-litellm-response-cost:' h.txt; done` 2. call 1: `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.00495456` with `{"usage":{"completion_tokens":2,"prompt_tokens":4762,"total_tokens":4764,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":4608},"cached_tokens":4608},"cached_via_details":4608}` 3. call 2: `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.00495456` with `{"usage":{"completion_tokens":2,"prompt_tokens":4762,"total_tokens":4764,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":4608},"cached_tokens":4608},"cached_via_details":4608}` Llama 3.3 70B publishes no cached-input discount, so a warm call costs the same as a cold one. What changes is the rate, $1.04 per 1M rather than the bucket's $0.90, and the cached count reaching `prompt_tokens_details`. The prefix was cold on both Before calls and warm on both After calls, which the counts show. Every model this branch adds also got its own live call: 21 of 24 answered, and each one billed at exactly its mapped rate, which is the check that the size buckets no longer shadow the entries. The three that did not answer are provider-side rather than litellm: `Kimi-K2.6` is listed but not serverless on this account, `LFM2.5-8B-A1B` returns 503 and no longer appears in `/v1/models` at all, and the pre-existing `Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-tput` entry whose output rate this branch corrects is retired from serverless. `Qwen3.6-Plus`, `Qwen3.7-Plus` and `Qwen3.7-Max` are streaming-only and were confirmed over a stream. The reasoning double-count is the one fix with no proxy-visible before and after, because a streamed response flushes its headers before the usage chunk arrives, so `x-litellm-response-cost` is empty for streams on both sides. It shows up three other ways. On the wire, `curl -N https://api.together.ai/v1/chat/completions -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3.7-Plus", ..., "stream":true, "stream_options":{"include_usage":true}}'` returns `"completion_tokens":140` beside `"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":134,"text_tokens":140}`, where Qwen3.7 Max sends the disjoint shape instead. In the per-model sweep, both Plus models went from a mismatched computed cost to a matching one. And the arithmetic is pinned by a unit test. ## Type 🆕 New Feature 🐛 Bug Fix 🧹 Refactoring ## Caveats (if any) - basedpyright not run locally; left to CI - Qwen3.6/3.7 Plus and 3.7 Max are streaming-only - Kimi-K2.6 needs a dedicated endpoint on some accounts - Llama 3.3 70B and Gemma 4 31B spend rises to published rates - Cache-rate fallback touches every provider, raising previously free hits - api.together.xyz still works; only the default moved - Rerank untouched, still ignores a custom api base - `max_output_tokens` omitted where Together publishes no cap ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(proxy): forward anthropic 429 rate-limit headers on /v1/messages
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - 429s from Anthropic-protocol backends drop `retry-after` - `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-status` is also stripped on 429 - Claude Code then retries a rejected quota forever How it solves it: - `/v1/messages` now forwards upstream 429 response headers - Anthropic-native headers pass through unprefixed to the client - Unsafe headers (cookies, CORS, framing) stay stripped ## User Flow Before: a developer using Claude Code against a LiteLLM gateway backed by an Anthropic-compatible model hits a quota 429 and their client retries endlessly 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the full `anthropic-beta` header and a body that trips the backend's weekly/monthly quota 2. The backend replies 429 with `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-status: rejected` and `retry-after: 287441` 3. The gateway returns 429 to Claude Code, but the response has neither `retry-after` nor `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-status` 4. Claude Code reads the bare 429 as a transient throttle and keeps re-sending the request in a tight loop After: the same 429 carries the two headers through, so Claude Code recognizes the rejection and stops 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the same `anthropic-beta` header and body 2. The backend replies 429 with `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-status: rejected` and `retry-after: 287441` 3. The gateway now returns 429 with `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-status: rejected` and `retry-after: 287441` present on the response 4.
